quiz.q: A bank's security team must detect suspicious traffic between application VMs in the same subnets for forensics, but its change board forbids any component that could add latency or drop production packets. Which control fits best?
choices: A Cloud NGFW Enterprise rule that sends all east-west traffic to a firewall endpoint with a deny action in the security profile
A Cloud Armor policy on the external load balancer with preconfigured rules applied to every request that reaches the application
A hierarchical firewall policy with goto_next rules that deny every protocol not explicitly listed between the application tiers
A Cloud IDS endpoint with Packet Mirroring over the application subnets, with alerts sent to the security team
quiz.explain: Cloud IDS inspects mirrored copies, so production traffic is untouched, and it sees intra-subnet traffic. NGFW intrusion prevention is inline and can drop packets, Armor sees only traffic entering through the load balancer, and firewall rules cannot detect threats in allowed traffic.

days.recap: Custom-mode VPC with planned ranges, Shared VPC for central control, hierarchical policies plus secure tags, Cloud IDS to detect (mirrored copies) and NGFW Enterprise to block inline, load balancer by scope and protocol, Cloud NAT out, Private Google Access for Google APIs (restricted VIP with VPC Service Controls).

days.title: Configuring Storage: Allocation, Access, Transfer, Retention, Lifecycle and Backup

concepts.heading: Allocation and Performance: Capacity Versus IOPS
concepts.body: Storage configuration starts by separating what you need to hold from how fast you need to reach it. With Persistent Disk, performance grows with disk size, so a 500 GB database that needs high IOPS can force you to buy capacity you never use. Google Cloud Hyperdisk breaks that link: you set IOPS and throughput per volume independently of capacity and can change them while the volume is in use, and Hyperdisk Storage Pools let a team buy capacity and performance in bulk and share it across disks. Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability replicates synchronously across two zones for stateful workloads that must survive a zone loss. Local SSD is attached to the host and extremely fast but does not survive the VM being stopped or the host failing, so it holds caches and scratch data, never the system of record. For files shared by many VMs or GKE Pods, Filestore gives managed NFS. For training data that accelerators must read quickly, Managed Lustre is the parallel file system and a zonal Rapid bucket the low-latency object option.

concepts.heading: Access Control in Cloud Storage
concepts.body: Cloud Storage has two parallel permission systems, IAM and ACLs, and a request succeeds if either allows it, so a forgotten ACL can expose data that IAM never intended. Uniform bucket-level access switches ACLs off so that IAM alone decides, which makes audits simple. Managed folders add IAM policies on a prefix inside one bucket, which is the middle path between a bucket per tenant (strong separation, many buckets to administer) and project-level grants (far too broad). EHR Healthcare, storing attachments for many medical-office customers under one prefix each, would use uniform access plus a managed folder per tenant. Public access prevention blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers and can be enforced through the storage.publicAccessPrevention organization policy. When an outside partner without a Google account needs one object for a limited time, a signed URL works even under public access prevention, because it is a time-limited bearer credential created with a service account. Treat it like a password and share it only with its intended recipient.

concepts.heading: Moving Data In and Keeping Latency Low
concepts.body: Transfer design depends on volume, bandwidth and how often data changes. Storage Transfer Service moves data online from other clouds, on-premises file systems and between buckets, with scheduling and integrity checks, and fits recurring or large copies over a network that can carry them. Transfer Appliance ships a physical device when the data is too large or the link too slow for the deadline. Dedicated Interconnect makes sustained online transfer predictable. Latency is a location decision: put the bucket in the region where compute runs, use dual-region or multi-region when availability across locations matters more than the lowest latency, and use Cloud CDN for content read worldwide. Dual-region buckets replicate between two regions by default, and turbo replication is an optional setting for faster, more predictable replication of new data. A zonal Rapid bucket sits next to accelerators in one zone for the lowest latency, but the authoritative copy of valuable data belongs in a regional or multi-location bucket. Altostrat Media's large library would sit in a location chosen for its main processing region.

concepts.heading: Retention, Lifecycle and Growth
concepts.body: Four features sound alike and do different jobs. Soft delete keeps deleted or overwritten objects recoverable for a retention window, so it is the simple safety net against accidents. Object Versioning keeps noncurrent versions until you remove them, which suits rollback of a specific earlier generation but grows without bound unless a lifecycle rule deletes noncurrent versions by age or by count of newer versions. A plain age rule targets live objects too. A bucket retention policy blocks deletion and overwrite until an object reaches the retention age, and Bucket Lock makes the policy permanent, which is the answer for WORM-style compliance such as a health insurer's seven-year claim records. Lifecycle rules also move objects to colder classes as they age, and Autoclass does it automatically for objects with unpredictable access. Growth planning means lifecycle rules, monitoring bucket size and choosing classes by access pattern, because colder classes trade lower storage cost for minimum storage durations and retrieval fees. Cymbal Retail's overwritten supplier feeds are a classic case for versioning plus a noncurrent-version delete rule.

concepts.heading: Backup That Survives a Compromised Administrator
concepts.body: A backup stored in the same project and under the same credentials as the workload is only as safe as those credentials. Backup and DR Service protects Compute Engine VMs and disks, Filestore, VMware Engine VMs and managed databases such as Cloud SQL and AlloyDB. Backup plans link workloads to a backup vault and contain rules for frequency, window and retention. The vault is Google-managed, isolated storage that enforces write-once-read-many immutability and an optional minimum retention, so even a privileged user in the workload project cannot delete backups early. That is the ransomware-resilient design: policy-driven backups, immutable vault, separate security boundary. For VMs, choose application-consistent backups for databases that must restore to a clean state, and crash-consistent ones for stateless data. Disk snapshots and Cloud Storage versioning remain useful but are not a vault. Always test restores against the recovery time you promised; a backup never restored is only a hope. EHR Healthcare's MySQL and SQL Server databases, holding regulated records, fit the vault pattern.

examPoints: Hyperdisk lets IOPS and capacity be provisioned separately, while Persistent Disk ties performance to size.
Soft delete protects against accidents, versioning with a lifecycle rule supports rollback, and a locked retention policy is the compliance answer.
Immutable backup vaults in Backup and DR Service keep backups safe even from a compromised administrator in the workload project.

quiz.q: A law firm stores signed settlement documents in Cloud Storage. Regulators require that nobody, including project owners and security administrators, can shorten the retention period or delete documents for eight years. What should the architect configure?
choices: Object Versioning with a lifecycle rule that keeps noncurrent versions for eight years, combined with a long soft delete window
A bucket retention policy of eight years that is then locked with Bucket Lock, so it cannot be reduced or removed
IAM deny rules for the delete permission on the bucket, applied at the folder with an exception for the security team
A dual-region bucket with turbo replication, so a deleted object remains available in the second region for eight years
quiz.explain: A locked retention policy is permanent and blocks deletion and overwrite until each object reaches its age. Versioning and soft delete are recoverable but deletable, an IAM deny can be changed by administrators, and replication does not provide immutability.

quiz.q: A video platform's tenants upload to one bucket with a prefix per tenant. A partner agency needs to read only its own prefix with its own service account, and the security team wants no per-object grants. What is the best configuration?
choices: Enable uniform bucket-level access and grant the agency's service account a role on a managed folder for its prefix
Grant the role on the whole project and rely on object ACLs to hide the other tenants' prefixes from the agency
Create a signed URL for every object in the prefix and send the list of URLs to the agency each month
Enable public access prevention on the bucket, which limits each service account to the prefix of the same name
quiz.explain: Managed folders carry an IAM policy for a prefix, including objects written later, and need uniform access. Project-wide grants are too broad, signed URLs per object are operational toil, and public access prevention does not scope service accounts.

days.recap: Size capacity and performance separately (Hyperdisk), use uniform access plus managed folders, pick transfer by volume and deadline (online service or Transfer Appliance), protect data with soft delete for accidents, versioning plus a lifecycle rule for rollback, locked retention for compliance and immutable backup vaults.

days.title: Configuring Compute: Provisioning, Spot, GKE and Serverless Networking, VMware Engine and IaC

concepts.heading: Provisioning for Demand: Autoscaling and Capacity Choices
concepts.body: Compute is provisioned against demand shape. Managed instance groups create identical VMs from an instance template and scale them with an autoscaler. A reactive autoscaler works from live metrics, which is too late for an application that takes minutes to start; predictive autoscaling forecasts daily and weekly cycles and adds instances ahead of the rise, with the initialization period telling the autoscaler how long a new instance needs before its metrics count. Scheduled scaling suits known events, and reactive scaling still handles surprises on top. Sole-tenant nodes give dedicated physical servers when a license counts physical cores or when isolation from other customers is required, with node affinity placing VMs on them and logs showing which physical server was used. For stable demand, committed use discounts lower cost; for bursty work, on-demand and Spot. The design habit is to name the demand pattern first (steady, cyclical, spiky, batch) and only then pick the capacity model. EHR Healthcare, with spikes that caused outages, needs automatic scaling plus health checks.

concepts.heading: Spot VMs: Cheap Capacity That Can Disappear
concepts.body: Spot VMs use spare Compute Engine capacity at a deep discount, and Compute Engine can preempt them at any time, either stopping or deleting the VM according to the termination action. They cannot live migrate and carry no availability guarantee. They fit fault-tolerant, stateless or checkpointable work: batch rendering, CI workers, data processing and some training. Make the design resilient rather than hopeful. Put workers in a managed instance group so capacity is replaced when it returns, checkpoint progress to durable storage, handle the short shutdown window with a shutdown script, and keep components whose loss halts everything, such as a queue or coordinator, on standard VMs or managed services. In GKE, create a separate Spot node pool, taint it, and give only tolerant Pods a matching toleration and node selector, so databases and critical services stay on standard nodes. Autopilot can handle Spot Pods for you. Altostrat Media's transcoding tasks are a natural fit if each task is short and repeatable, while a stateful database is not.

concepts.heading: GKE and Serverless Networking
concepts.body: Private connectivity differs by platform. In a private GKE cluster nodes have only internal IP addresses; the control plane endpoint can be restricted with authorized networks so only listed ranges connect, and outbound internet access for nodes and Pods goes through Cloud NAT with the Pod ranges included. Private Google Access covers only Google APIs. Cloud Run reaches private IP resources such as Memorystore or on-premises systems through Direct VPC egress, which is recommended because instances take addresses from a subnet and there are no connector instances to run; Serverless VPC Access connectors are the older alternative and must be sized. Plan the subnet, since Direct VPC egress consumes addresses. Inbound control matters as much: Cloud Run ingress set to internal and Cloud Load Balancing makes an external Application Load Balancer the only internet front door, so Cloud Armor and Identity-Aware Proxy cannot be bypassed through the default run.app address. Choose Cloud Run for stateless containers with minimal operations, Cloud Run functions for event handlers, and GKE when you need Kubernetes control, which Altostrat Media and EHR Healthcare already have.

concepts.heading: Moving Virtual Machines: VMware Engine and Patching
concepts.body: Not every VM should be rewritten. Google Cloud VMware Engine runs the VMware stack (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, NSX and HCX) on Google Cloud bare metal, so tools, skills and processes carry over and VMs can be migrated with HCX in waves, often keeping their IP addresses. It needs private connectivity between the sites. For KnightMotives, gradually replacing mostly on-premises legacy systems, it lets VMs move first and keep their addresses; converting to Compute Engine or containers can follow. For VMs that stay, patching has two models. VM Manager provides OS patch deployment with schedules, rollout by zone and disruption limits, plus compliance reporting, and suits long-lived servers. For stateless tiers in a managed instance group, replace rather than patch: build a new image or template and run a rolling update, controlling surge and maximum unavailable, so every instance starts from the same tested image and rollback means pointing to the previous template. GKE adds release channels, maintenance windows and maintenance exclusions to keep upgrades flowing while avoiding a retailer's holiday sales period.

concepts.heading: Infrastructure as Code and Orchestration Choices
concepts.body: Repeatable environments come from declaring them in code. Terraform is the declarative standard, and Infrastructure Manager is the managed service that runs Terraform configurations from Cloud Storage or Git and tracks deployments and revisions. Cloud Deployment Manager reached end of support on 2026-03-31, so it is never the right answer for new work. One parameterized module can create development, staging, production and a per-customer environment, pull-request review gives change control, and re-applying the configuration corrects drift. Scripts and manual steps describe how, drift between environments, and repeat the misconfigurations that caused EHR Healthcare's past outages. For container orchestration, match the platform to the control needed: Cloud Run for stateless services without cluster management, GKE Autopilot for Kubernetes with Google managing nodes, GKE Standard when you need node-level control such as custom pools and Spot, and Compute Engine when the software requires a full VM. Consistent management of several Kubernetes environments is a requirement in two of the cases, so use fleet-wide policy and configuration rather than cluster-by-cluster changes.

examPoints: Spot VMs need a fault-tolerant design: managed instance groups, checkpoints and critical coordinators on standard capacity.
Cloud Run reaches private IP resources through Direct VPC egress, and ingress restricted to internal and load balancing forces traffic through the load balancer.
Use Terraform with Infrastructure Manager for repeatable environments, because Deployment Manager has ended.

quiz.q: A genomics company runs a nightly pipeline of 2,000 independent tasks that each take about 20 minutes and can be restarted from the start without harm. The job coordinator keeps the task queue in memory. The team wants the lowest compute cost. Which design is best?
choices: Run every component, including the coordinator, on Spot VMs in one managed instance group so that cost is minimized across the pipeline
Run workers on standard VMs reserved for a year and keep Spot VMs only as a standby in case the workers fail
Run workers on Spot VMs in a managed instance group and place the coordinator and queue on standard VMs or a managed queue service
Run workers on sole-tenant nodes so the preemption of a Spot VM cannot affect tasks that are already in progress
quiz.explain: Restartable independent tasks suit Spot workers, while the coordinator holding the queue is a single point whose loss stops everything and belongs on standard capacity or a managed service. All-Spot risks losing the queue, reserved VMs raise cost, and sole-tenant nodes do not stop preemption.

quiz.q: A startup's Cloud Run API must read from a Memorystore instance over private IP. The security team also requires that customers reach the API only through a global external Application Load Balancer with Cloud Armor. Which pair of settings meets both needs?
choices: Serverless VPC Access with the largest connector size, and ingress set to all so that the load balancer can still reach the service
Direct VPC egress into a subnet of the network, and ingress set to internal and Cloud Load Balancing for the service
A Cloud NAT gateway for the Cloud Run service, and ingress set to internal so the load balancer reaches the service
Private Google Access on the subnet, and ingress set to all with a Cloud Armor rule on the run.app address instead
quiz.explain: Direct VPC egress provides private outbound access to Memorystore, and ingress of internal and Cloud Load Balancing removes the direct run.app path so the load balancer is the only entry. Ingress set to all leaves a bypass, and Cloud NAT or Private Google Access do not reach private resources.

days.recap: Match capacity to demand shape (predictive autoscaling for slow starts), use Spot only with resilient design and a standard coordinator, give private clusters Cloud NAT and authorized networks, use Direct VPC egress for Cloud Run, move VMware with HCX when time is short, and declare environments with Terraform and Infrastructure Manager.

days.title: Configuring AI Workloads: Agent Platform Pipelines, Data Integration, GPUs, TPUs and Consumption Models

concepts.heading: Pipelines Make ML Repeatable and Auditable
concepts.body: An ML pipeline on Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI) is a directed acyclic graph of containerized tasks connected by declared inputs and outputs. It is serverless, can be scheduled, and turns ad hoc notebook work into repeatable continuous training. The architectural benefit is lineage: as the pipeline runs, ML Metadata records executions, parameters and artifacts, so everything that contributed to a model, the datasets, the code version and the parameters, can be traced, and a model registered in Model Registry links to the run that produced it. Altostrat Media requires recommendation models that are auditable and explainable, so training belongs in pipelines rather than manual scripts. Pipelines also cache: before a step runs, the system looks for an earlier execution with the same interface (inputs, output definition and component specification) and reuses its outputs. That is efficient, but a step reading changing data through an unchanging query looks identical every night and returns stale results. Pass a date or snapshot ID as a parameter, or disable caching for just that task.

concepts.heading: Data Integration: Orchestrate in the Pipeline, Process in the Engine
concepts.body: Do not make a pipeline task hold terabytes in one container. A pipeline task can be a thin step that starts a job on another engine, waits for it and passes the output on. Joins and aggregations on warehouse data belong in BigQuery. Record-level parsing at scale, including streaming and Apache Beam logic, belongs in Dataflow. Large Spark or Hadoop jobs belong in Managed Service for Apache Spark. The pipeline keeps ordering, caching, parameters and lineage across all of them while each engine scales independently. For serving features to models, Feature Store on Agent Platform lets you keep feature data in BigQuery tables or views, which act as the offline store, and serve the latest values online at low latency from the same definitions used in training, which reduces training-serving skew. This avoids both putting analytic query latency in the request path and operating a second copy of the data. Cymbal Retail's catalog enrichment would pair BigQuery for supplier data with a pipeline that calls a generative model and then a human review step.

concepts.heading: Choosing Accelerators: GPUs and TPUs
concepts.body: AI Hypercomputer is Google Cloud's integrated infrastructure for AI: accelerators, networking, storage and software. The first choice is the accelerator. TPUs are designed for large matrix operations, with high-bandwidth memory and chips connected in slices that scale a workload with little code change. They suit models dominated by matrix computation and without custom operations in the main training loop. They are a poor fit for models with many custom C++ TensorFlow operations or custom PyTorch or JAX operations that must run partly on CPUs. GPUs are the flexible choice when custom kernels or operations that TPUs do not support are essential, and when the team's code and ecosystem assume CUDA. Both are supported on Agent Platform training. The decision is rarely about raw speed; it is about whether the model's operations map to the hardware and what the team can port. KnightMotives, with autonomous-driving work and obsolete AI infrastructure, should validate the model on a small TPU or GPU configuration before committing to a large cluster.

concepts.heading: Consumption Models: Matching Capacity to the Job
concepts.body: Obtaining GPU capacity is a planning problem as well as a technical one. On-demand capacity is best-effort with no discount and no assurance. Spot is deeply discounted and immediate if available, but can be preempted at any time, so only checkpointed, fault-tolerant jobs belong there. Flex-start fits short jobs of up to seven days that can wait for capacity; it is best-effort, discounted on supported series and not preemptible, so it suits fine-tuning, small pre-training, batch inference and simulation. Standard reservations give assurance for critical general GPU workloads. Future reservations cover large clustered training: capacity blocks reserve densely allocated capacity for a future date and time and suit pre-training foundation models, optionally with a commitment of a year or more for discounted rates, and calendar mode reserves clustered capacity for up to 90 days. A quota increase is only permission to ask, not capacity. The decision facts are: can the job be preempted, can it wait, how long does it run, and how tightly coupled is the cluster.

concepts.heading: Feeding the Accelerators
concepts.body: An accelerator waiting for data is expensive idle time, so storage is part of the design. Google Cloud Managed Lustre is a fully managed parallel file system for AI and HPC with POSIX compliance, high throughput and low latency, which existing training tools use without changes. It integrates with Compute Engine and GKE for mounting and with Cloud Storage for fast managed transfers in and out. A common pattern keeps durable data in Cloud Storage and stages the working set into Managed Lustre for training. For object-based access in one zone, a zonal Rapid bucket in the same zone as the accelerators gives the lowest latency, with hierarchical namespace and uniform bucket-level access required; the authoritative copy of valuable artifacts belongs in a regional or multi-location bucket. Checkpointing to durable storage is what makes cheaper, interruptible capacity usable. KnightMotives, training large autonomous-driving models on GPU nodes, would stage the working set into Managed Lustre rather than have every node stream many small files from object storage.

examPoints: Pipelines capture lineage in ML Metadata, which is the evidence auditors need, and caching must be controlled when the underlying data changes.
Let pipeline tasks start BigQuery, Dataflow or Spark jobs for heavy data work and keep the pipeline as the orchestration layer.
Match consumption to the job: Spot for fault-tolerant, Flex-start for waitable jobs under seven days, future reservations for large planned clustered training.

quiz.q: A bank fine-tunes a model for three days on an eight-GPU VM. The job has no checkpointing, cannot be restarted midway, and may start up to a day later than requested. The team has no reservation and wants a discount. Which option fits?
choices: Spot VMs, because the discount is the largest and the job can simply be restarted if capacity is reclaimed during the run
On-demand GPUs with a quota increase requested, because quota guarantees that capacity will be available at the start time
A future reservation in calendar mode for ninety days, because every GPU job should have reserved capacity before it starts
Flex-start provisioning, because it is non-preemptible and discounted for short jobs that can wait for capacity
quiz.explain: Flex-start suits waitable, non-preemptible jobs of up to seven days at a discount. Spot can be preempted and the job cannot restart, a quota increase grants no capacity, and a ninety-day future reservation is oversized for a three-day job.

quiz.q: A retailer's nightly retraining pipeline on Agent Platform ingests a BigQuery table through a fixed query string. The model has not improved for a week even though new rows arrive daily, and the ingest step is reported as skipped. What is the best fix?
choices: Pass the snapshot date as an input parameter to the ingest step so its interface changes each night, or turn off caching for that task
Move the ingest query into a notebook that an engineer runs by hand each morning before the scheduled pipeline run starts
Turn off caching for the entire pipeline job, which is the only way to make any single step run again on schedule
Increase the machine size of the training step, since the ingest step is skipped because the training container is too small
quiz.explain: Execution caching matches on the step's interface, and an unchanged query looks identical, so the earlier output is reused. Making the changing fact part of the interface or disabling caching for that one task fixes it. Disabling it for the whole job works but also reruns costly steps, and a manual notebook gives up repeatability.

days.recap: Train in pipelines for lineage (and watch step caching), orchestrate in the pipeline but process in BigQuery or Dataflow, choose TPU or GPU by whether the operations map to the hardware, buy capacity by preemptibility and wait tolerance (Spot, Flex-start, future reservations), and feed accelerators with Lustre or Rapid.

days.title: Google AI APIs, Gemini Enterprise, Notebooks and Model Garden: Choosing the Right Tool and Domain 2 Review

concepts.heading: Prebuilt APIs: Match the Input Type
concepts.body: Google's prebuilt AI APIs give a ready result with no model to train, and the first design step is matching the input. Cloud Vision API analyzes images: labels, objects, faces, landmarks, text and explicit content. Video Intelligence API analyzes stored or streamed video: shot changes, object tracking, logos, speech transcription and explicit content detection, with results tied to time segments, which is why Altostrat Media would use it to find harmful scenes in its library. Speech-to-Text converts audio to text, and Natural Language API analyzes text for entities, sentiment and syntax. Document AI extracts structured data from documents. Speech-to-Text has three request styles: synchronous for short audio, batch for long stored audio, and streaming over a bidirectional gRPC stream with interim results for live captions. These APIs analyze content; they do not create it. Choose them when categories are common and speed matters. If the classes are proprietary, such as a manufacturer's own part numbers, a prebuilt label API will not know them and you need a custom model or a prompted multimodal model, validated on labeled examples.

concepts.heading: Analyze Versus Generate
concepts.body: A frequent exam trap is using an analysis API for a generation need. Generative image models on Agent Platform can create images from text prompts, edit an image within a mask you define, and upscale images. Cymbal Retail's goal of producing image variations and background edits from supplier photos is generation, not analysis, so Vision is the wrong tool. Because generated content can be wrong or off-brand, the case study already requires a human-in-the-loop review interface before catalog updates; that review step is the right control, and a grounding source such as the supplier data reduces errors in generated attributes and descriptions. The same distinction applies to text: Natural Language API classifies and extracts, while a Gemini model summarizes, rewrites and converses. For the architect, state the verb in the requirement: detect, extract and classify point to prebuilt APIs or custom models; draft, summarize, rewrite and converse point to generative models. Cost and latency also differ, so use the simplest tool that satisfies the verb.

concepts.heading: Gemini Enterprise and Gemini Notebook Enterprise
concepts.body: Gemini Enterprise is a managed work platform. You connect Google and third-party data sources such as Google Drive, SharePoint and Jira; ingested data goes into data stores that apps use to serve search, answers, actions and agents, and the assistant is grounded in that content under the organization's security and compliance settings. Employees can build single- and multi-step agents without code with Workflow Builder, Google provides agents such as Deep Research, and admins can register custom agents, including those built with the Agent Development Kit and hosted on Agent Runtime, agents using the Agent2Agent protocol, and Dialogflow conversational agents, so existing investments are not rebuilt. Gemini Notebook Enterprise (formerly NotebookLM Enterprise, still the name in the exam guide) is narrower: users add chosen sources such as PDFs, Docs, Slides and URLs to a notebook, and answers are grounded only in those sources, inside your Google Cloud project. Use a notebook for focused analysis of a fixed document set, such as a compliance team's policies, and Gemini Enterprise for organization-wide assistants and agents connected to many systems.

concepts.heading: Model Garden and Building on Agent Platform
concepts.body: Model Garden is the library in Agent Platform where you discover, test, customize and deploy models from Google and partners. It groups foundation models, fine-tunable models and task-specific solutions, and deployment and serving follow one consistent pattern, with third-party models scanned before deployment. The decision is control versus operations. Hosted model APIs minimize operational work and suit most applications. Open-weight models from Model Garden are the choice when licensing, data control or customization demand it, for example a team that must fine-tune on private data and serve from a dedicated endpoint under its own project; then you pay for the compute of the endpoint and own the tuning and evaluation. Building agents and applications directly on Agent Platform gives maximum flexibility but costs engineering time, which a company with non-developer teams may not have, so it chooses Gemini Enterprise. For customer-facing chat such as Altostrat Media's support assistant, pair the model with grounding and with Model Armor screening of prompts and responses. Prefer managed, grounded options before custom models.

concepts.heading: Domain 2 Consolidation: Provision Against Requirements
concepts.body: Domain 2 asks you to turn a design into a configured, running solution. Use this checklist. Network: link type and topology set availability, Cloud Router priority steers paths, Shared VPC and custom mode ranges prevent collisions, firewalls use hierarchy and secure tags, IDS detects and NGFW blocks, and the load balancer follows scope and protocol. Storage: separate capacity from IOPS with Hyperdisk, use uniform access and managed folders, choose soft delete, versioning with lifecycle, or locked retention by the question being asked, and use immutable vaults for backups. Compute: name the demand shape, use Spot with resilient design, give private clusters Cloud NAT and authorized networks, use Direct VPC egress for Cloud Run, VMware Engine when time is short, and Terraform with Infrastructure Manager for environments. AI: pipelines for lineage, TPU or GPU by operations, consumption model by preemptibility and wait tolerance, prebuilt API by input type, Gemini Enterprise for connected assistants, Model Garden for control. When two answers both work, prefer the managed option that meets the stated reliability and cost priorities.

examPoints: Detect, extract and classify call for prebuilt APIs or custom models, while draft, edit and summarize call for generative models.
Gemini Enterprise is for organization-wide connected assistants and agents, and Gemini Notebook Enterprise is for focused analysis of a chosen document set.
Choose Model Garden open models when licensing, control or customization require it, otherwise use hosted APIs and managed products.

quiz.q: A utilities company wants to extract invoice numbers, dates and totals from thousands of supplier PDFs with different layouts into BigQuery. The team has no ML engineers and wants a managed service. Which choice fits best?
choices: Train a custom image-classification model on Agent Platform using a labeled sample of the invoices
Use Document AI to extract structured fields from the documents and write the results to BigQuery
Use Video Intelligence API on the PDFs so that text segments and time stamps are returned for each page
Use Gemini Notebook Enterprise and ask it to list the fields for every invoice one document at a time
quiz.explain: Document AI is the prebuilt service for extracting structured data from documents without ML staffing. A custom classifier does not extract fields, Video Intelligence analyzes video, and a notebook is for interactive analysis of a document set, not bulk extraction into a warehouse.

quiz.q: A 5,000-person firm wants employees to search and ask questions across Drive, SharePoint and Jira, and wants department managers to build their own simple agents without writing code. Which choice meets this with the least engineering?
choices: Gemini Notebook Enterprise, with one notebook per department holding exports of the connected systems' content
A custom retrieval application on Agent Platform with its own connectors, front end and agent framework
Model Garden open-weight models fine-tuned on exports from the three systems and served on a dedicated endpoint
Gemini Enterprise, connecting the three data sources and using Workflow Builder for no-code agents
quiz.explain: Gemini Enterprise connects Google and third-party sources, grounds the assistant in them and offers no-code agent building. Notebooks cover fixed document sets, a custom build costs engineering time, and fine-tuned models do not provide connectors or governed access to live content.

days.recap: Match the API to the input type (Vision, Video Intelligence, Speech-to-Text, Document AI), separate analysis from generation, use Gemini Enterprise for connected agents, notebooks for fixed document sets, Model Garden when control is needed, and review Domain 2 as network, storage, compute, AI.

days.title: Identity and Access: Resource Hierarchy, Roles, Separation of Duties, Service Accounts and Federation

concepts.heading: The Hierarchy as the Control Plane
concepts.body: IAM allow policies and organization policies inherit downward through organization, folders and projects. A grant on a folder reaches every project below it, and new projects start with the folder's controls, so the hierarchy is the main design tool for security. Model business units and environments as folders: a holding company with three business units, each with production and non-production, gets a folder per unit and an environment folder inside, with stricter policy on production. Grant roles to groups, not individuals, so access review means reviewing group membership. Google recommends folders under one organization rather than several organizations, because separate organizations have no central visibility and every guardrail must be copied. IAM decides who can act; organization policy decides which configurations are allowed for everyone. A policy set high gives new folders the guardrail automatically, and a lower node can carry an explicit exception, whereas re-applying controls folder by folder leaves gaps. For KnightMotives, with past breaches and EU compliance, central guardrails on the organization are the first design move.

concepts.heading: Roles, Least Privilege and Separation of Duties
concepts.body: Prefer predefined roles; basic roles of any generation (Admin, Writer, Reader and the legacy Owner, Editor and Viewer) are too broad for production. Custom roles fill gaps at organization or project level. To shrink an over-granted estate, use role recommendations, which analyze permissions a principal actually used and suggest a smaller role, and verify the effect with Policy Simulator before applying, so nobody loses access they need. For rare high-privilege tasks, Privileged Access Manager grants temporary elevation through an entitlement that defines roles, duration and whether justification or approval is required, and audit logs show who held access when; standing Owner rights for database administrators are the anti-pattern. Separation of duties means no single identity can both change and approve, or administer and use: the security team administers keys, the service uses them; one group manages networks, another deploys applications. IAM deny policies add guardrails that override allow, with exception principals such as a break-glass group, and can attach to the organization, a folder or a project.

concepts.heading: Protecting the Root: Super Admins and the Organization
concepts.body: A Cloud Identity or Workspace super admin can do almost anything in the identity layer, including granting the Organization Administrator role, so treat these accounts as the root of trust. Do not use them for daily work: give each administrator a separate account for that purpose, enforce multi-factor authentication with physical security keys, and keep the number of super admins small but more than one so one lost account is not a lockout. Use a private admin group with the Organization Administrator role, or a subset, for day-to-day management. Organization Administrator is an access-management role: it grants roles and sees the hierarchy, but creating folders and projects needs Folder Creator and Project Creator. A new organization grants Project Creator and Billing Account Creator to the entire domain, so tighten that to a platform group. Alert on SetIamPolicy calls through Cloud Logging and rehearse account recovery. For people from an external identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID or EHR Healthcare's Active Directory, Workforce Identity Federation maps them to a workforce pool without creating Google accounts for each person.

concepts.heading: Service Accounts: Fewer Keys, Narrower Identity
concepts.body: A service account is an identity for software. Google advises avoiding service account keys whenever possible, because a key is a long-lived credential that can leak from a repository, a log or a laptop. Attach a service account to the resource instead (a VM, Cloud Run service or function), and on GKE use Workload Identity Federation for GKE to bind Kubernetes service accounts to IAM identities. Give each workload its own service account with only the roles it needs, rather than one shared account that grows into a master key. When a person or system must act as a service account temporarily, use impersonation: the caller needs a role such as Service Account Token Creator on the target to mint short-lived credentials, or the Service Account User role to attach it to a resource, and the activity is logged under both identities. Impersonation also lets developers test with a service account's permissions without downloading a key. Organization policy can block key creation across the organization, with a deliberate exception on a single legacy folder rather than weakening the rule everywhere.

concepts.heading: Workload Identity Federation for External Systems
concepts.body: Software running outside Google Cloud, such as a SaaS CI/CD platform, an on-premises job or another cloud, should not hold a service account key. Workload Identity Federation lets it authenticate with its own identity provider. The external system presents a short-lived token (OIDC or SAML), a workload identity pool provider validates it, and attribute mappings copy claims such as repository, branch or account into attributes. Access is then granted either directly to the federated principal or by letting it impersonate a service account. An attribute condition, or a grant bound to a principalSet for one repository, makes sure other repositories in the same CI account cannot use the identity. No key is stored, so nothing can leak, and credentials expire on their own. Remember the pair: Workforce Identity Federation is for people, Workload Identity Federation is for software. Altostrat Media's CI/CD for containers on GKE in Google Cloud and on-premises should deploy through federation and impersonation, and restrict image deployment further with Binary Authorization.

examPoints: Hold guardrails in the hierarchy with groups, folders and organization policies, and use deny policies for rules nobody may break.
Replace standing privilege with Privileged Access Manager, and shrink broad roles with role recommendations checked by Policy Simulator.
Avoid service account keys: attach accounts, impersonate for temporary access, and use Workload Identity Federation for external software.

quiz.q: A software company deploys to Google Cloud from a hosted CI platform outside Google Cloud. A service account key is stored as a pipeline secret, and the security team wants no long-lived credentials, with only the main repository of one project able to deploy. What should the architect do?
choices: Rotate the key every week and store the new key in Secret Manager, with the CI platform reading it through its own service
Create a workload identity pool and provider for the CI platform and grant access only to the one repository
Give the CI platform's account the Service Account Token Creator role on every service account in the production folder
Export the key to a hardware security module owned by the CI vendor and restrict the key's use with an IP allowlist
quiz.explain: Workload Identity Federation exchanges the CI platform's short-lived token for Google credentials, and an attribute condition limits it to one repository, so no key exists. Rotation still leaves a long-lived key, broad token-creator rights over-grant, and an HSM-held key is still a key.

quiz.q: Database administrators need Owner-level rights on production projects for maintenance about twice a month. Today the rights are permanent. The CISO wants elevated access only when needed, with a record of who held it and why. Which design fits best?
choices: Keep the permanent grant but require two-step verification for the administrators' accounts and review the group quarterly
Replace the Owner role with the legacy Editor role on production projects, because Editor cannot change IAM policies
A Privileged Access Manager entitlement with a time limit and required justification, and removal of the standing grant
Move the administrators to a separate organization so that their rights can never apply to the main production projects
quiz.explain: Privileged Access Manager gives time-boxed elevation with justification and audit trail, which removes standing privilege. Two-step verification does not shorten the exposure window, Editor is still broad, and a separate organization breaks central control.

days.recap: Use the hierarchy, groups and organization policy for central control, least privilege with recommendations and Privileged Access Manager, protected super admins, keyless service accounts (Token Creator to impersonate, Service Account User to attach), Workforce federation for people and Workload federation for software.

days.title: Keys, Secrets, Data Protection and Audit Logging

concepts.heading: Choosing where the key material lives
concepts.body: Encryption at rest is on by default, so the architect's question is who controls the key. With Google-managed encryption Google handles everything. With customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) the data service uses a key in Cloud KMS that you control: you set who may use it, how it rotates and when it is disabled. A software key and a Cloud HSM key both live inside Google's infrastructure, and Cloud HSM adds hardware protection. Cloud EKM is different: the key material stays in an external key manager that you operate outside Google Cloud, Google cannot use it unless you allow it, and you can withdraw access at any time. The price is availability, because the external manager is now on the critical path, and if you lose keys you hold outside Google, Google cannot recover the data. For example, a regulator that demands keys in the insurer's own custody points to EKM, while a company that only wants audit evidence of key use is well served by CMEK with a software or HSM key. Choose the weakest control that meets the stated requirement.

concepts.heading: Many projects, many keys: Autokey and org policy
concepts.body: Manual CMEK does not scale. Someone plans key rings, creates keys, grants each service agent the encrypt and decrypt role, and developers wait. Cloud KMS Autokey automates this: an administrator enables an Autokey configuration on a folder, and when a developer creates a protected resource such as a disk, dataset or bucket, a key handle triggers on-demand creation of a suitably specific key in a designated key project, with service agent roles granted. Developers need no KMS admin rights, and the security team keeps visibility. To make CMEK mandatory, two organization policy constraints work together: gcp.restrictNonCmekServices requires CMEK for listed services, and gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects limits which projects may supply keys. Both apply only to resources created after the policy, so existing resources need separate remediation. For KnightMotives, which has suffered breaches and must meet EU data protection rules, Autokey plus these constraints on the data platform folder gives strong, uniform encryption governance without slowing teams.

concepts.heading: Separating key administration from key use
concepts.body: Cloud KMS splits managing a key (create, rotate, disable, set IAM) from using it (encrypt, decrypt). Cloud KMS Admin can manage but cannot decrypt, and CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter can use but cannot manage. A sound design keeps keys in a dedicated key project owned by the security team, gives the security team the admin role only, and gives the service agent of each data service the use role on exactly the key it needs. Then no human group can both control and read the data, which is what auditors mean by separation of duties; Owner for everyone defeats it. Rotation is a second design lever. Automatic rotation on a schedule, for example every 90 days, is the recommended practice and some standards require it; rotation creates a new key version but does not re-encrypt existing data, and old versions stay active until destroyed. Key destruction is scheduled with a delay, then permanent, which makes crypto-shredding possible: give each tenant or person a key, and destroying it makes every copy, including backups, unreadable. Plan this per tenant only where the contract needs it, because many keys cost management effort.

concepts.heading: Secrets and data in use
concepts.body: Passwords, API keys and certificates do not belong in container environment files, repositories or general buckets, because every copy spreads the risk and nothing records who read what. Secret Manager stores them as versioned secrets with IAM on each secret. A workload's service account gets the Secret Accessor role on only the secrets it needs, rotation means adding a new version that workloads pick up when they read the latest, and access can be written to Data Access audit logs. Kubernetes Secrets in each cluster duplicate values per cluster and cannot give one rotation and audit story across GKE and Cloud Run. Cymbal Retail, with MySQL, SQL Server, Redis and MongoDB plus many batch integrations, has exactly this credential sprawl to avoid. Encryption covers data at rest and in transit, but data in use sits decrypted in memory. Confidential VMs use hardware-based confidential computing to keep memory encrypted and isolated from the host and hypervisor, typically with no code change, which suits two firms pooling sensitive records for joint analysis. For finer access inside BigQuery, policy tags give column-level control from a single table.

concepts.heading: Audit logging that an auditor will trust
concepts.body: Cloud Audit Logs have several types. Admin Activity logs record configuration changes and are always on. Data Access logs record reads of resource data and are off by default for most services (some BigQuery logs excepted), so the architect must enable them for Cloud Storage or Cloud SQL when the question is who read the patient file. Two decisions make the trail trustworthy. First, centralize: configure at the organization or folder so new projects are included, and route logs through an aggregated sink to a log bucket in a separate security project that the logged engineers cannot reach. Second, protect and retain: retention is set per bucket, and locking the bucket makes its retention permanent. The Required bucket holds Admin Activity and System Event logs and has fixed retention; the Default bucket is configurable. Log buckets exist only in projects, so an organization-level sink routes to a bucket in the security project. EHR Healthcare, with regulatory compliance and consistent logging and retention to deliver, would answer who-read-the-file with Data Access logs plus an aggregated sink, not VPC Flow Logs, which see network flows but not API users.

examPoints: A requirement that keys stay outside Google and be revocable points to Cloud EKM with its availability dependency, while hundreds of projects needing CMEK without KMS admin rights points to Cloud KMS Autokey.
Separation of duties on keys means the security team holds key admin only and the service agent holds the encrypter/decrypter role only, and an Owner role for everyone breaks it.
Who read this object needs Data Access audit logs, which are off by default, sent through an aggregated sink to a locked bucket in a separate security project.

quiz.q: A hospital group stores imaging archives in Cloud Storage. Its compliance officer wants proof that no one in the platform team can both change the encryption key settings and decrypt the archives, and wants the key lifecycle owned by security. Which design meets this?
choices: Create the keys in a project owned by the security team, grant them Cloud KMS Admin only, and grant the Cloud Storage service agent the encrypter/decrypter role on that key
Create the keys in the platform team's project, grant them Owner so they can rotate quickly, and rely on the audit logs to show that nobody decrypted data by hand
Use Google-managed encryption for the archives and give the security team the object viewer role, so that they can monitor access and detect misuse after it happens
Create one key per platform engineer, grant each engineer the admin and decrypt roles on it, and review the grants every quarter during the access recertification
quiz.explain: Key management and key use are separate permissions. Security administers the key without being able to decrypt, and only the service agent decrypts at run time, so no human group holds both. The Owner choice contains both permission sets, so detection by logs does not create separation.

quiz.q: Altostrat Media's pipeline reads a database password from a file committed in a configuration repository, and the same value is copied into three GKE clusters. Security wants one place to rotate it and an audit trail of reads, for workloads on GKE and Cloud Run. What should the architect propose?
choices: Encrypt the repository file with a key stored beside it, and ask each team to replace its copy during the next release cycle
Store the password in Secret Manager, grant each workload's service account access to only that secret, and rotate it by adding a new version
Create a Kubernetes Secret in each cluster, restrict namespace access, and write a runbook that lists the clusters to update in turn after each change
Put the password in a private Cloud Storage bucket as a text file and mount the bucket into every container that needs it, using one shared account
quiz.explain: Secret Manager gives a single source of truth with per-secret IAM, versions for rotation and auditable access across GKE and Cloud Run. Per-cluster Kubernetes Secrets duplicate the value and give no common rotation or audit trail.

days.recap: Pick the key location from the requirement: CMEK for control, HSM for hardware assurance, EKM when keys must live outside Google, Autokey for scale. Split key admin from key use, keep credentials in Secret Manager, protect memory with Confidential VMs, and make Data Access logs tamper-resistant.

days.title: Security Controls: Perimeters, Guardrails, Firewall Policy and Context-Aware Access

concepts.heading: VPC Service Controls: a perimeter around Google APIs
concepts.body: IAM answers who may call an API, but a caller who passes IAM can still copy data to any bucket the API allows, and a stolen credential passes the same check. VPC Service Controls adds an independent layer: projects placed in a service perimeter cannot have protected services read from or written to resources outside it, even by principals with the right roles. Both checks must pass, so use it with IAM, not instead of it, and not instead of firewalls, which govern VM traffic rather than calls to Google APIs. Legitimate exchanges are opened with explicit ingress rules (outside callers coming in) and egress rules (protected resources reaching out), which name identities, services and methods. Perimeters can run in dry run mode, where violations are allowed but logged, so a bank wrapping 40 production projects can read the logs, model real flows such as a partner feed as rules, and enforce when the log is clean. Google notes some metadata may still be reachable, so do not promise zero leakage. Protecting Agent Platform inside a perimeter keeps models and prediction requests from leaving it.

concepts.heading: Organization Policy versus IAM and deny policies
concepts.body: IAM allow policies grant roles to principals. Organization Policy is different: it restricts what resources may be configured, by constraint, and it inherits down the hierarchy from the organization through folders to projects. Set a strict default at the top and carve out an exception lower, such as a legacy folder where a vendor product still needs service account keys. Typical constraints cover allowed resource locations, which services may be used, whether service account keys can be created, and the CMEK requirements. A third tool is the IAM deny policy, which is evaluated before allow, attaches to an organization, folder or project, names principals and permissions, and supports exception principals such as a break-glass group. Use deny when the rule is about who cannot do something regardless of grants a project owner might add, and use organization policy when the rule is about what can exist. A holding company with three business units places both on folders so each new project starts protected, and grants roles to groups so access reviews cover membership rather than individuals.

concepts.heading: Hierarchical firewall policies and layered network defense
concepts.body: VPC firewall rules are set by whoever administers a network, so a central security team needs a rule that application teams cannot override. Hierarchical firewall policies attach to the organization or a folder and are evaluated before VPC-level rules, top down. An organization rule can deny or allow definitively, for example denying SSH and RDP from the internet to every VM network, and a goto_next action hands everything else to lower levels so teams keep their own rules. EHR Healthcare, running several Kubernetes environments, benefits from one mandatory baseline plus team freedom. Firewalls control traffic by network attributes. Cloud NGFW intrusion prevention adds layer 7 inspection through firewall endpoints and security profiles, covering east-west traffic, whereas Cloud IDS only detects and alerts from mirrored copies. The design principle is defense in depth: network policy for VM paths, perimeters for API paths, IAM and deny for identity, and organization policy for configuration. A question that asks which single control blocks everything is usually a trap; ask which path the threat takes.

concepts.heading: Identity-Aware Proxy: access by identity, not network position
concepts.body: A classic approach to internal web applications puts them behind a VPN, so network position equals trust. Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) inverts that: requests reach the application only after IAP authenticates the user and checks IAM, so access is granted per group and per application and can add context such as device or location through access levels. The app trusts the signed identity header IAP adds and needs no custom login code. The policy is managed centrally, outside the application, which suits an internal HR application on Compute Engine behind an external Application Load Balancer that employees and a few contractors use from home. IAP also protects a backend only if the backend cannot be reached around it, so pair it with firewall rules or ingress settings that force traffic through the load balancer. IAP can also front TCP administration of VMs without external addresses, removing the need to expose SSH to the internet. Choose IAP when the target is a specific application or VM and the question mentions users, groups and no VPN.

concepts.heading: Chrome Enterprise Premium and context-aware access
concepts.body: Context-aware access means the decision depends on who the user is, the security posture of the device and where the request comes from, expressed as access levels. Chrome Enterprise Premium extends Chrome's enterprise security with that context-aware access plus data protection controls in the browser, such as limits on uploads, downloads and copy and paste, and threat protection against malware and phishing. Because it works through the browser, it fits users on devices the company does not own. KnightMotives' dealers, who have no equipment budget and so must use devices they already own for the CRM and inventory tools, are the example: no device purchase is required, and an access level can require device security posture, an approved location or a verified identity. Pick the tool by what the requirement emphasizes. A single internal web app and a group of users point to IAP, a boundary against data leaving Google-managed services points to VPC Service Controls, mandatory network rules point to hierarchical firewall policies, and mixed SaaS and web access from unmanaged devices points to Chrome Enterprise Premium.

examPoints: Roll out a VPC Service Controls perimeter in dry run, read the logs, add ingress and egress rules, then enforce, and remember that the perimeter complements IAM and firewalls without replacing either.
A rule that no one may do X even if granted it points to an IAM deny policy, and a rule about which resources or locations may exist points to Organization Policy.

Choose the access tool by the target: IAP for specific internal apps by identity, Chrome Enterprise Premium for unmanaged devices and SaaS, and hierarchical firewall policy for mandatory network rules.

quiz.q: A research institute stores genomic data in BigQuery. An auditor notes that a researcher with valid roles could export a table to a bucket in a personal project, and the institute cannot find every legitimate partner flow. What is the safest way to add an exfiltration control?
choices: Replace the researchers' roles with a custom role that removes export permissions, then rely on the Cloud Audit Logs to catch any use of other APIs
Place the projects in a VPC Service Controls perimeter in dry run, study the logged violations, add ingress and egress rules, and then enforce
Enforce a perimeter on all projects immediately, and ask partners to report broken integrations during the first week after enforcement
Add a hierarchical firewall policy that denies all egress from the projects' VM networks to addresses outside the corporate range
quiz.explain: A perimeter blocks copying to resources outside it even for principals with valid IAM roles, and dry run reveals legitimate flows before enforcement can break them. Firewall policy governs VM traffic, not calls to the BigQuery or Cloud Storage APIs.

quiz.q: EHR Healthcare's platform team must guarantee that no VM network in any project accepts RDP from the internet, while application teams stay free to manage their own other rules. Which approach fits?
choices: An organization-level hierarchical firewall policy with a deny rule for that traffic and goto_next for everything else
A VPC Service Controls perimeter around all projects with an egress rule that blocks the remote desktop protocol from reaching the VMs
A VPC firewall rule created in each project's network by the application teams, reviewed each quarter by the security team
An IAM deny policy on the compute.instances.get permission so that engineers cannot find the VMs to connect to
quiz.explain: Hierarchical firewall policies are evaluated before VPC rules and cannot be overridden below, and goto_next leaves the rest to the teams. Perimeters protect Google API calls, not VM network traffic, and per-project rules can be edited by their owners.

days.recap: Layer the controls by path: IAM for who, VPC Service Controls for data leaving Google APIs, Organization Policy and deny policies for guardrails, hierarchical firewall policy for network baselines, IAP and Chrome Enterprise Premium for context-aware access. Dry run before enforcing.

days.title: Software Supply Chain and Securing AI Workloads

concepts.heading: Securing the pipeline that builds your software
concepts.body: A software supply chain is every step from source code to a running workload, and an attacker needs only one weak step. The architect's controls follow the flow. Build in a managed, isolated service such as Cloud Build, and when builds must reach private dependencies, use a private pool that is peered into your VPC so internal artifact servers need not be exposed to the internet. Store the result as an immutable artifact in Artifact Registry and promote that same artifact through environments by digest, because a tag can be moved to another image and a digest identifies exact content. Keep environment settings out of the image, in configuration and Secret Manager references. Grant the pipeline its own service account with only the roles the job needs, and prefer Workload Identity Federation for pipelines that run outside Google Cloud rather than exported keys. Altostrat Media, which delivers containers to GKE clusters in the cloud and on premises with central management, wants exactly this single, auditable path. The theme is provenance: you should be able to say who built what, from which source, and what checks it passed.

concepts.heading: Scanning and gating with Artifact Analysis
concepts.body: Artifact Analysis provides software composition analysis. Automatic scanning in Artifact Registry is triggered by every image push, includes language packages, and keeps vulnerability information updated as new vulnerabilities are discovered, so an image that was clean last month can gain findings without being rebuilt. Findings can also appear in Security Command Center next to other risks. On-demand scanning is a one-time scan you start yourself, which does not update afterwards and so does not replace continuous scanning. The architectural point is shifting left and making the result a gate: a scan nobody acts on is only a report. Pipelines such as Cloud Build can check results before promoting an image, and Artifact Analysis also stores metadata, such as the fact that an image passed an integration test or a vulnerability check, that later stages can rely on. A team shipping several times a day should scan at push, fail the pipeline on unacceptable severity, and keep a process for patching base images, since fixing the base image is usually cheaper than patching every application.

concepts.heading: Binary Authorization: enforcing what may run
concepts.body: Scanning finds problems, but something must stop a bad image reaching production. Binary Authorization enforces a policy at deploy time on supported platforms such as GKE and Cloud Run: only images that satisfy the policy are admitted. The common pattern uses attestations, signed statements from an attestor that a stage was completed, for example that Cloud Build built the image from approved source or that a scan found no unacceptable vulnerabilities. Policies can differ by stage, so production is stricter than test. Artifact Registry controls who can push, and Binary Authorization controls what can run, which are different questions. It does not prescribe your process; it enforces the process you define. After a supply chain scare, Altostrat Media would require a build attestation for production clusters, which blocks an image pushed by hand from an engineer's laptop even if the engineer has push rights. Limits to remember: it is an admission-time control, so it does not detect vulnerabilities that appear in already-running images; that remains the job of continuous scanning and Security Command Center.

concepts.heading: Sensitive Data Protection: find, then de-identify
concepts.body: Before protecting data you must know where it is. Sensitive Data Protection discovery scans BigQuery, Cloud Storage and other supported sources across a project, folder or organization and generates data profiles with the information types found and sensitivity and risk levels, kept current as data changes; results can feed Security Command Center or a catalog and drive policy tags and access decisions. Inspection finds values in text, and de-identification transforms them. The technique decides what analysts can still do. Redaction, replacement and masking destroy the original and cannot be reversed. Cryptographic tokenization, such as deterministic encryption or format-preserving encryption, gives the same token for the same input so joins still work, and can be reversed with a key wrapped in Cloud KMS, which suits analysts who need behavior across records without seeing identities. Bucketing generalizes values such as age into ranges, and date shifting moves dates consistently so intervals survive. Re-identification risk analysis, with measures like k-anonymity, tests whether quasi-identifiers such as ZIP code and birth year still single people out. Pick the transformation from the analysis the data must still support.

concepts.heading: Model Armor and secure AI deployment
concepts.body: Generative AI adds threats that network controls do not see: prompt injection, jailbreaks, harmful output and leakage of sensitive data. Model Armor screens prompts sent to a model and responses it returns. A template sets the filters and the confidence thresholds: prompt injection and jailbreak detection, responsible-AI categories, malicious URLs, and sensitive data detection through Sensitive Data Protection with optional redaction. Thresholds trade protection against false positives, so test them with a representative set of good and bad prompts. Because screening happens in a service you control, it applies consistently across applications and models, which matters when customers can paste free text into a support chat like Altostrat's. Securing the deployment also uses familiar controls. Put Agent Platform inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter so training data, models and prediction requests cannot leave it, and note that private connectivity options alone do not remove public reachability. Use CMEK where required, least-privilege service accounts for agents, audit logging, and a human review step before AI output changes critical data, as Cymbal Retail plans for catalog updates.

examPoints: Supply chain questions are answered as a chain: managed build, immutable artifact promoted by digest, automatic scanning, and Binary Authorization attestations to enforce what may run.

Sensitive Data Protection technique follows the needed analysis: tokenization keeps joins and is reversible, masking or redaction is irreversible, and risk analysis checks quasi-identifiers before release.
Model Armor screens prompts and responses at run time, while VPC Service Controls, CMEK, IAM and audit logs secure the AI platform itself, and the two answer different threats.

quiz.q: After a supplier library was found to contain a serious flaw, a company's security team wants production GKE clusters to run only images that its official pipeline built and that passed a vulnerability check. Engineers still have permission to push to the registry. Which control enforces this?
choices: Restrict who can push images to Artifact Registry by removing the writer role from every engineer's account, so that only the build account pushes
Run an on-demand vulnerability scan on the production images every quarter and email the findings to the owners of each affected service
Require attestations from the build pipeline and the scan in a Binary Authorization policy that is enforced on the production clusters
Rebuild each image from source in every environment, so that the production image never depends on a build from an earlier stage
quiz.explain: Binary Authorization decides at admission time what may run, using attestations that the pipeline and scan produced, so a manually pushed image is rejected even if the engineer can push. Registry permissions control pushing, not running, and quarterly scans are neither continuous nor enforcing.

quiz.q: A marketing team wants to analyze customer chat transcripts in BigQuery to see how often each customer returns, without the analysts learning anyone's name or email. A small privacy team may need to re-link records for a legal request. Which approach fits?
choices: Mask names and emails with a fixed character so that every record shows the same value in those columns, then hand the table to analysts
Replace each name and email with a deterministic cryptographic token and keep the key in Cloud KMS for the privacy team only
Delete the name and email columns and the free text from the dataset, then publish only an aggregate table to the analysts
Move the transcripts to a bucket in another region and grant analysts access to that copy with a viewer role on the bucket
quiz.explain: A deterministic token gives the same output for the same person, so return-visit analysis still works, and the key allows authorized reversal. Masking and deletion make records unlinkable and irreversible, and relocating the data protects nothing.

days.recap: Secure the chain from build to run: private pools, immutable artifacts by digest, Artifact Analysis scanning, Binary Authorization attestations. Use Sensitive Data Protection to find and de-identify data with the technique the analysis needs, Model Armor for prompts and responses, and VPC-SC and CMEK around AI.

days.title: Compliance: Regulation, Residency, Sovereignty and Audit Evidence

concepts.heading: Shared responsibility and what certifications prove
concepts.body: Google Cloud publishes independent certifications, attestations and audit reports, for example SOC 1, SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001 and PCI DSS, through its compliance resource center and Compliance Reports Manager. They cover controls that Google operates: facilities, infrastructure and the services it runs. Compliance of a customer's own service is shared. The customer remains responsible for how it configures and uses the services: identities and access, data classification, network and application settings, logging and change processes. An auditor therefore expects evidence of both layers, the provider's report and the customer's controls. A developer who says the checkout application is automatically PCI compliant because Google Cloud is certified is wrong, and the architect should explain that a shared responsibility matrix shows which requirements Google covers. The same applies to HIPAA: there is no certification program for it, and a Business Associate Agreement covers only listed products, so protected health information must stay in covered services. Compliance questions on the exam are architecture questions: which design makes the customer's half provable and keeps scope small. Legal interpretation stays with counsel.

concepts.heading: Reducing scope for card data, health data and children's data
concepts.body: Scope drives audit effort. PCI DSS applies to systems that store, process or transmit cardholder data and to systems that secure and log access to them, so the best design keeps card data in as few places as possible. Isolate the card environment in its own project and VPC with minimal firewall flows, log and monitor access, and use tokenization or a hosted payment page. Where card numbers appear in call transcripts, Sensitive Data Protection can redact or mask them before they reach analytics, so those systems stay outside the card environment; Cymbal Retail, whose call-center agents key in orders, is a likely candidate. For protected health information, use an organization policy that restricts which service APIs a folder may use, so only BAA-covered products can be enabled by mistake, and avoid pre-GA services for PHI. For services directed to children, as with COPPA, design for data minimization, an isolated project with narrow IAM, retention limits through expiration and lifecycle rules, and a way to find and delete one child's records, including derived tables.

concepts.heading: Residency, sovereignty and Assured Workloads
concepts.body: Data residency is where data is stored and processed. The resource locations organization policy constraint restricts the locations in which supported resources can be created, so a company can allow only EU locations and block drift. Granularity matters: a BigQuery dataset in the EU multi-region stays in EU locations but does not guarantee a specific country, so a rule that data stay in Germany needs a regional dataset, and dataset location cannot be changed after creation. Sovereignty goes further and covers who can access data and under whose control. Assured Workloads applies a control package to a folder, enforced with organization policy and other features and monitored for violations. EU packages set data location controls, and a package with support controls limits support access to EU-based personnel, which is the kind of requirement KnightMotives' EU data protection compliance can raise. Check each package's supported products list: services not listed have not met all its controls, so restrict usable services with the Restrict Resource Service Usage policy. Access Approval requires your administrator to approve Google staff access, and Access Transparency logs it.

concepts.heading: Preventive and detective controls, and evidence that cannot be altered
concepts.body: A compliance design uses both kinds of control. Preventive controls stop the action: organization policy constraints refuse a resource in a forbidden location at API time. Detective controls find what exists or has drifted: Security Command Center monitors for misconfigurations, vulnerabilities and threats, compares resources with standards such as NIST, HIPAA, PCI-DSS and CIS, reports posture drift and exports findings. Not every rule can be a constraint, so combine them and route findings to a response process. Evidence must also survive the people it describes. A Cloud Storage retention policy that is locked with Bucket Lock cannot be reduced or removed even by a project owner, which gives write-once, read-many behavior for records that must be kept for years; logs reach it through sinks, including aggregated sinks at organization level. Log bucket location is fixed at creation and buckets default to the global location, so for EU-only log data configure default resource settings at the organization or folder before projects are created, because existing buckets are not moved. EHR Healthcare's need for consistent retention across projects is solved the same way.

concepts.heading: GDPR roles, erasure and sharing data safely
concepts.body: Under GDPR the customer is typically the controller, who decides purposes and means, and Google is the processor acting on the customer's instructions under the data processing terms, with standard contractual clauses for transfers outside the EU where needed. The legal basis, retention and application design remain the customer's. Designing for erasure is an architecture task because personal data is copied into backups, analytics and derived tables. Keep a stable subject key and a catalog of where each person's data lives so deletion jobs can reach every copy, and consider crypto-shredding for the most sensitive fields: encrypt with a per-person key in Cloud KMS and destroy it so even backups become unreadable. When analysts abroad need insights from EU telemetry, compute in the data's location and release only aggregated or de-identified results, because queries run where the data lives and copying raw data to another location may break residency. For sharing health records externally, use de-identification into a separate destination dataset and measure re-identification risk. Whether the result satisfies a regulation is a decision for the privacy officer and counsel.
