examPoints: Provider certifications are the base and not the answer: the customer must still configure and evidence its own controls, and the design goal is to keep audit scope small.

Residency is about location and is enforced with the resource locations constraint at the right granularity, while sovereignty adds who may access data and is addressed by Assured Workloads packages, Access Approval and key control.
Pair preventive controls such as organization policy with detective ones such as Security Command Center, and keep evidence in locked retention buckets that no project owner can alter.

quiz.q: A German health insurer must keep customer data within Germany. A team created a BigQuery dataset in the EU multi-region, and the compliance reviewer flags it. What should the architect do?
choices: Keep the dataset because the EU multi-region already guarantees that the data is stored inside the Federal Republic of Germany and needs no more work
Change the dataset location to a Germany region in place, and rely on the next scheduled query to move the existing tables across to it
Recreate the dataset in a Frankfurt region, copy the data, and add a resource locations organization policy that limits new resources to Germany
Add a column-level policy tag to the sensitive fields so that analysts outside Germany are unable to read those columns of the dataset
quiz.explain: The EU multi-region keeps data in EU locations but not in one country, and a dataset's location cannot be changed after creation, so the data must be copied into a regional dataset. The organization policy stops new resources drifting out. Policy tags control who reads columns, not where data is stored.

quiz.q: A payments startup runs its checkout on Google Cloud. A developer argues that because Google Cloud is certified for PCI DSS the startup's whole estate is automatically compliant. How should the architect respond and reduce the audit effort?
choices: Agree, because the provider's attestation transfers to every application that is hosted on its certified products
Disagree and explain shared responsibility, then isolate card-handling systems in their own project and VPC and tokenize card data early
Disagree and recommend moving the checkout on premises, where the company controls every layer needed for the assessment
Agree for storage and compute but require a separate certification for networking, because only that layer needs customer work
quiz.explain: Google's certification covers the controls it operates, and the customer remains responsible for its application's compliance. Isolating and tokenizing shrinks the scope that must be assessed. Moving on premises would take on more responsibility, not less.

days.recap: Provider certifications are the base, shared responsibility is the rule. Shrink scope, enforce location with organization policy at the right granularity, add Assured Workloads and Access Approval for sovereignty, combine preventive and detective controls, and keep evidence in locked buckets. Design for erasure and share only de-identified data.

days.title: SDLC, CI/CD, Troubleshooting, Testing and Disaster Recovery Drills

concepts.heading: Designing CI/CD: build once, promote, control the release
concepts.body: A delivery pipeline should make the safe path the easy path. Build and test with Cloud Build, store an immutable image in Artifact Registry, and promote that same artifact through staging and production, referring to it by digest, because rebuilding per environment can pull different dependency versions and make production differ from what was tested. Settings that vary by environment live in configuration and Secret Manager, not in the image. Cloud Deploy then delivers to a series of targets in a defined sequence: a release is created from the built images, each promotion is a rollout, and a target can require approval before promotion, publishing a Pub/Sub message that an approval workflow can consume. It also records who promoted what, giving traceability. Altostrat Media, which needs CI/CD for containers with central management across Kubernetes in the cloud and on premises, wants exactly this central, repeatable path. Release strategies such as canary or traffic shifting limit the blast radius and make rollback fast. When the build needs private dependencies, a Cloud Build private pool reaches them over the VPC without opening them to the internet.

concepts.heading: Testing and validation across the lifecycle
concepts.body: Shifting left means moving quality and security checks earlier, where defects are cheaper to fix. For infrastructure defined as code in Terraform or Infrastructure Manager, a pipeline can create the same stack for each pull request, run tests against a production-like environment and destroy it afterward, so cost follows use and environments do not drift. Validate the plan, not only the code: policy checks against the proposed changes fail a pull request that would create a public database, a preview shows the real diff to a human approver, and organization policies reject non-compliant resources as a backstop. Dependency vulnerabilities are caught by automatic scanning at push and used as a gate. Controlled production techniques such as canary releases and feature flags complement pre-production testing but do not replace it. A generative AI component needs a different kind of test because output varies: build an evaluation set with known-correct answers across verticals, measure what the requirement states, such as valid attributes in the catalog structure and hallucinated attributes, agree acceptance thresholds in advance, and keep human review before updates, as Cymbal Retail would for catalog enrichment.

concepts.heading: Troubleshooting by hypothesis and evidence
concepts.body: The exam rewards a method: read the symptom, form a hypothesis from evidence, test it with a change-free tool, and only then change something. Symptoms often point to a specific cause. If a load balancer backend is unhealthy while the service answers from inside the VPC, the probe ranges may be blocked by firewall rules, because health checks come from Google-operated ranges. If VMs without external addresses time out only on Google APIs in a new subnet, Private Google Access is probably off for that subnet. Failures only under burst load through Cloud NAT suggest port exhaustion, solved with more addresses or ports. Pods stuck Pending although the node pool maximum is far away suggest scale-up blocked by quota or address space, visible in noScaleUp events. Errors about too many database connections during a serverless spike point to pooling and instance caps, not a bigger machine. When two teams say their side is fine across a hybrid link, Connectivity Tests analyze the end-to-end path without changing anything, as EHR Healthcare would. Resist the answer that opens firewalls or rebuilds links, which adds risk and hides the cause.

concepts.heading: Root cause analysis and observability
concepts.body: Root cause analysis builds a timeline from evidence. Many outages follow a change, and Admin Activity audit logs record configuration changes and are always on, so putting the changes next to the metric that moved shows which change came first. Averages hide slow outliers, so for a rise in tail latency use Cloud Trace to see which downstream span is slow and correlate trace and span identifiers with log entries to learn why. Error Reporting groups errors by root cause and shows when a group first appeared, so a new group tied to a release signals a regression. During an incident, mitigate before investigating: roll back or shift traffic away from the new revision, which keeps the stack traces and logs for later analysis. Afterward run a post-incident review that records the timeline, immediate cause and systemic causes, and fix the system, not only the symptom: if a firewall rule was edited by hand, the lasting fix is review and infrastructure as code. EHR Healthcare's past outages from misconfiguration, spikes and inconsistent monitoring fit this pattern.

concepts.heading: Service provisioning and testing disaster recovery
concepts.body: A project factory built as infrastructure as code takes a few inputs and produces a standard project: the right folder with its organization policies and IAM, billing link, labels, a budget with alerts, approved APIs and baseline groups. A catalog of approved Terraform blueprints, deployed by a pipeline under its own service account, lets non-engineers request a standard environment, such as one for KnightMotives' dealer tools, while holding no infrastructure permissions. Self-service is not self-privilege: guardrails stay in the hierarchy. Disaster recovery needs the same discipline. Patterns run from cold to warm to hot by how readily they recover: a pilot light keeps only the replicated data and core running, with the rest defined as code and launched on demand, so it fits an hours-level recovery on a limited budget. But RTO and RPO are only claims until measured. Run game days that perform the real failover with real operators, including identity, DNS or load balancer changes and application checks, and restore backups into an isolated environment, because healthy replication shows data moving, not that the application serves requests. Backup for GKE backs up configuration and volumes for restore into another cluster.

examPoints: Build once and promote the same immutable artifact through environments with Cloud Deploy approvals, rather than rebuilding for each stage.
A troubleshooting answer starts with evidence from a change-free tool such as Connectivity Tests, Cloud Trace or logs, and avoids opening firewalls or resizing before a hypothesis exists.
A disaster recovery plan is proven only by measured failover exercises and restore tests, and the DR pattern follows the RTO, RPO and budget.

quiz.q: Cymbal Retail's checkout service on GKE has a rising 99th percentile latency, while average latency looks normal. Logs show no errors. Which action most directly finds where the slow requests spend time?
choices: Increase the node pool size so that the cluster has more headroom for the slowest requests during peak hours, then watch for any change
Review the average CPU utilization of each node and compare it with the figures from the previous week to spot any change
Use Cloud Trace to inspect slow request spans across services and open the logs correlated with those trace identifiers
Roll back to the previous release immediately and compare customer complaints with the old latency numbers over the next day
quiz.explain: Tail latency needs request-level evidence. Traces show which downstream span is slow, and correlated logs explain why. Adding nodes or reading averages changes or measures things without a hypothesis, and a rollback with no sign of regression is a guess.

quiz.q: Altostrat Media's ingestion system must recover within a few hours of a data center loss, with limited budget. Its data is replicated continuously to Google Cloud. After designing a pilot light, what is the best way to gain confidence in the design?
choices: Review the replication dashboard weekly and record in the plan that the recovery target has been met while the lag stays low
Run a failover exercise with the real operators, create the infrastructure from code, and measure the recovery time and data loss
Increase the replication frequency and assume that the recovery objectives will follow from the lower lag between the sites
Document the runbook thoroughly and have a second architect review it against the written objectives before it is signed off
quiz.explain: Objectives are targets until a real exercise measures them, and drills reveal missing permissions, stale steps and dependencies. Healthy replication and a reviewed runbook do not show that the application starts and serves requests from the recovery site.

days.recap: Build once, promote by digest, and gate releases with Cloud Deploy. Test early with environments as code, plan checks and evaluation sets. Troubleshoot from evidence, mitigate before RCA, automate provisioning, and prove disaster recovery with measured game days and restore tests.

days.title: Business Processes: Stakeholders, Change, Skills, Decisions and Customer Success

concepts.heading: Stakeholders: identify, analyze, engage
concepts.body: Stakeholders are the people and groups affected by a project or able to influence it: sponsors, application owners, security and compliance, operations, finance, customers and partners. A missing stakeholder usually appears as a late requirement, and late requirements are expensive. Identify the groups, including those with veto power such as compliance; analyze them by influence and interest to decide who is consulted, who approves and who is informed; then engage the high-influence groups early, record their requirements and agree how decisions are made, for example with a RACI. A compliance team that announces its data location and logging needs two weeks before a payment migration cutover is the failure case; bring them in at the start. When stakeholders disagree, treat their statements as positions and look for the requirement behind each. A security lead insisting on private-only access and a product owner demanding a launch in six weeks may both be satisfied by a narrower first release on private connectivity with a lighter pre-approved path for standard changes. The architect facilitates, makes trade-offs explicit in risk, cost and schedule, and escalates the decision, not the argument, to the accountable executive.

concepts.heading: Change management: people adopt change
concepts.body: Technical success does not guarantee adoption. Established change practice covers a clear case for change, sponsorship, early user involvement, training, support and adoption measures. Pilots are central: a small group of willing users finds problems when they are cheap to fix, and their success becomes a reference for others. KnightMotives is rolling out a CRM and sales tool to dealers who have no equipment budget, after an unreliable online ordering system strained them. A pilot with a few dealers, a browser-based tool that runs on equipment they already own, and waves that expand when the pilot meets agreed measures, with the old way kept until the new way is proven for each group, will rebuild trust. A big-bang switch with penalties raises risk and resistance. Resistance is information: employees who fear a virtual agent will replace them need transparency, a role in shaping it, a visible future role and reskilling. Change control for deployments should also be proportionate: approve routine pipeline deployments once as a standard change checked automatically by tests and policy, and reserve human review for novel or hard-to-reverse changes.

concepts.heading: Skills readiness and operating-model fit
concepts.body: A cloud program is a people change as much as a technology change. A readiness plan starts with a skills gap analysis comparing current skills with those the target operating model needs, such as cluster operations, observability, IAM and incident handling. It continues with role-based training and certification paths, a sandbox where mistakes are cheap, and support through the transition from a partner, internal champions or a platform team that pairs with the team through the first production releases. The operational excellence pillar adds a design lever: reduce the skills needed by matching the platform to the team. A four-person team with no container experience running a stateless HTTP API with variable traffic fits Cloud Run, which is serverless and manages servers and scaling, better than GKE, where upgrades, node pools and policy are skills to build, and far better than self-managed Kubernetes on VMs. Choose the simplest platform that meets the requirements, knowing a container can move to GKE later. EHR Healthcare faces a hard lease deadline and already runs containers on several Kubernetes clusters, so standardizing how they are managed fits its team better than adding another new platform during the move.

concepts.heading: Decision making: reversibility, evidence and records
concepts.body: Not every decision deserves the same rigor, and a useful split is reversible versus hard to reverse. A dashboard tool can be swapped with modest effort, so decide quickly and time-box a trial. The region that will hold regulated customer data affects compliance, latency, cost and later migrations, so it deserves analysis against requirements, compliance and legal input and a recorded decision. Three weeks of debate on the first and none on the second signals a process problem. When opinions conflict and facts are missing, convert the disagreement into a question you can answer. A time-boxed proof of concept tests the riskiest assumptions, such as scale, multi-region writes and schema fit, with realistic data, and success criteria are agreed first: throughput, latency, consistency, operating effort, team skills and cost. Seniority or a general claim that one product scales further are not requirements. Record the outcome in an architecture decision record, a short document kept near the code with context, requirements, options considered, the decision and its reasons, and with new records that cite earlier ones when the decision changes. This speeds onboarding and troubleshooting.

concepts.heading: Customer success and stakeholder communication
concepts.body: Customer success means customers reach the outcome they bought the service for. Infrastructure health is an input, and the measures of success describe what the customer experiences: business KPIs such as onboarding time, feature adoption, retention and support satisfaction, together with service level indicators and objectives for the availability and latency of the interfaces the customer uses. Feedback loops, such as ticket trends and satisfaction scores, reveal problems dashboards miss. Linking technical objectives with customer KPIs lets an architect show that a design change, for example better onboarding automation, moved a result the customer cares about. EHR Healthcare onboards insurers one after another and must show the cloud move helps them, so time to onboard an insurer and the availability of its interfaces are the evidence. Communication is part of the job. Tailor it: finance wants forecast versus budget and commitments, the sponsor wants outcomes, risks and decisions needed, operations wants runbooks and readiness, security wants control evidence. Agree success criteria and decision rights early, report against them, and be honest about risks, since bad news early is cheaper than bad news late.

examPoints: Late requirements usually mean a missed stakeholder, so identify and analyze them by influence and interest and engage the high-influence groups, such as compliance, before design is fixed.
Adoption is earned through pilots, champions, waves, training and removing barriers, and forced big-bang cutovers or mandates raise risk.
Match decision effort to reversibility, settle conflicts with a time-boxed proof of concept against agreed criteria, and record the result in an architecture decision record.

quiz.q: A company has asked its fifteen development teams to adopt a new CI/CD platform within six months. A previous tool mandate failed and the teams distrust central decisions. Which rollout is most likely to succeed?
choices: Announce a hard cutover date, shut the old pipelines on that day and track pipeline runs per team for the executive report
Start with a few teams whose needs are simple, name respected champions, improve the platform from feedback and share lead-time results
Ask the central platform team to migrate every repository itself over a weekend so that teams never need to change their habits
Publish detailed written standards and a compliance checklist, then audit each team at the end of the quarter for conformance
quiz.explain: Adoption grows from peers and measured benefit: a pilot wave, champions and outcome metrics such as lead time. A hard cutover repeats the earlier failure, activity counts can be gamed, and a central weekend migration or audit-only approach does not build ownership.

quiz.q: A data team lead wants Spanner for a new transactional service, while the application team prefers Cloud SQL for familiarity. Neither side has measured the expected write volume or regional spread. What should the architect do?
choices: Choose Spanner because the more scalable product removes the risk of outgrowing the database in the future and avoids a later migration
Choose Cloud SQL because the team's familiarity lowers operating effort and outweighs any speculative growth that nobody has measured
Run a time-boxed proof of concept on agreed criteria such as throughput, latency, consistency and cost, and record the decision
Ask the most senior engineer to decide, and document the reasoning only if the decision is later challenged by someone
quiz.explain: When opinions replace facts, convert the disagreement into a testable question with success criteria agreed beforehand, then record the result. Scalability alone and familiarity alone are positions, not requirements, and a seniority decision gives no evidence.

days.recap: Treat people and process as design inputs: identify stakeholders and engage compliance early, find the requirement behind each position, run pilots and waves for change, close the skills gap or choose simpler platforms, decide with evidence and ADRs, and measure customer success with KPIs and SLOs.

days.title: Cost Optimization, CapEx and OpEx, Business Continuity and Domain 4 Review

concepts.heading: From CapEx to OpEx
concepts.body: On premises, hardware is a capital expense: money is spent up front for capacity that must cover the peak and depreciates over years. In Google Cloud most services are an operating expense: you pay for what you use, when you use it, and can add or remove capacity quickly. The cost optimization pillar of the Well-Architected Framework treats this as a change of discipline, not just accounting. A manufacturer closing two data centers will welcome the end of large purchases, but the finance director must be warned that variable spend can grow without a hardware approval to slow it, so the plan includes budgets and alerts that notify owners when spend crosses thresholds, labels, folders and projects that attribute spend to teams and products for showback or chargeback, and a regular review. Steady parts of the load can be committed at a lower rate, while variable or spiky load stays on demand so the company does not pay for idle peak capacity. For Cymbal Retail, which wants lower data-center cost while it modernizes a mix of on-premises and cloud, the point is to retire on-premises capacity as workloads move, otherwise the company pays twice.

concepts.heading: Attribution first, then remove waste
concepts.body: Cost control has two steps. Attribution answers who spends what: labels on resources, a project and folder structure that matches teams and products, and an export of detailed billing data to BigQuery so finance can group, filter and chart cost by label or project. Without it, forty teams sharing a few projects produce a growing bill nobody can explain. Waste removal answers what is not needed: the Recommender service analyzes utilization and suggests actions such as resizing over-provisioned VMs or deleting idle resources, and acting on them is the fastest saving that needs no commitment. Only after waste is removed should the company commit to steady load, otherwise it locks in the waste. Other waste patterns come from the pillars: development and test environments that run around the clock although developers use them during working hours can be scheduled to stop, or defined as code and created on demand, since stopped VMs do not incur compute charges although their disks do. Cost optimization never justifies dropping a risk control or the availability a requirement states. Altostrat Media lists reliability and cost as its top priorities, so every saving must be checked against the availability target.

concepts.heading: Matching the purchase model to the workload
concepts.body: Google Cloud offers several ways to pay for compute, each a trade-off. On-demand is the most flexible and has the highest list rate. Committed use discounts trade a one-year or three-year commitment for a lower rate, as spend-based or resource-based commitments, and suit steady, predictable, always-on load. Spot VMs offer deeply discounted capacity that Google can reclaim at any time, so they suit fault-tolerant work that checkpoints and restarts. The architect reads the workload description for the clue. If Altostrat Media re-transcodes its video archive as batch jobs that restart from a checkpoint and have flexible deadlines, those fit Spot VMs, while a continuously serving user-facing service does not tolerate interruption and fits on-demand capacity covered by commitments for the steady baseline. Storage has its own levers: lifecycle rules, Autoclass and classes matched to access frequency reduce cost while keeping high availability, a stated Altostrat need. Serverless platforms such as Cloud Run scale to zero, which removes idle cost for spiky workloads. Sustainability follows the same logic, since running fewer, better-utilized resources lowers both cost and footprint.

concepts.heading: Business continuity: objectives, impact and testing
concepts.body: Business continuity planning keeps critical functions running through a disruption. The reliability pillar asks you to set recovery objectives from business need before choosing technology. RTO is how long a service may be down and RPO is how much data, measured in time, may be lost. A business impact analysis ranks services by the cost of an outage in patient care, contracts and regulation, so objectives differ by tier: a clinical record lookup cannot be down, while a reporting batch can wait hours. Tighter objectives need more redundancy and cost more, so a single design for dozens of services wastes money or leaves gaps. EHR Healthcare's 99.9% availability target for customer-facing systems should be applied to those systems with a tiered design. A written plan such as restoring an order system in another region within an hour is a hypothesis until a real exercise measures it, and exercises find secrets, DNS, IAM bindings or images that exist in only one region. Migrations need their own continuity plan: a rehearsal, a go or no-go checkpoint, a rollback path with the source kept in sync, and decommissioning only after a full business cycle.

concepts.heading: Domain 4 consolidation: reading the question
concepts.body: Domain 4 is about the process around the technology. Look for the verb in the stem. If the topic is delivery, think build once, immutable artifact, Cloud Deploy promotion with approval, environments as code and policy checks on the plan. If it is a failure, think symptom, hypothesis, change-free evidence, mitigate before RCA and a post-incident review that fixes the system. If it is people, think stakeholder analysis, pilots, champions, skills gap analysis, simpler platforms and communication tailored to the audience. If it is a decision, think reversibility, proof of concept with agreed criteria and an architecture decision record. If it is money, think attribution, then Recommender waste removal, then commitments for steady load, Spot VMs for interruptible work and schedules for idle environments. If it is continuity, think business impact, RTO and RPO per tier, the cold, pilot light, warm or hot pattern that fits the budget, and measured failover. The usual wrong answers are a bigger instance, a mandate, a meeting-heavy approval process, a single global design, or a plan that was never tested. Choose the answer that satisfies the stated requirement at the lowest risk and cost.

examPoints: Cost optimization starts with attribution through labels, folder structure and billing export to BigQuery, continues with Recommender waste removal, and only then adds commitments for steady load.

Match purchase model to workload: committed use for steady baselines, Spot VMs for fault-tolerant batch that checkpoints, on-demand for the unpredictable, and scheduled shutdown for idle test environments.
Recovery objectives come from a business impact analysis per service tier, tighter objectives cost more, and the plan counts only after a measured exercise.

quiz.q: A retailer's cloud bill is growing, and about forty teams share five projects. Finance cannot tell which team causes the growth, and engineers suspect many oversized VMs. The CFO asks for a first step that saves money without long commitments. What should the architect do?
choices: Buy three-year committed use discounts for the current compute total, so that the highest discount applies to everything
Move every team to Spot VMs, because the discounted capacity will reduce the compute bill regardless of workload type
Add labels and a project structure per team, export billing data to BigQuery, and act on Recommender sizing suggestions
Ask each team to estimate its own spend monthly and compare the estimates with the invoice at quarter end
quiz.explain: Attribution shows who spends what, and Recommender finds oversized and idle resources, a saving that needs no commitment. Committing now would lock in waste, Spot VMs would break workloads that cannot be interrupted, and self-estimates give no evidence.

quiz.q: EHR Healthcare must reach at least 99.9% availability for customer-facing systems and is choosing disaster recovery designs for dozens of internal services. A reporting job can be down for a day, while the claims lookup service cannot. What is the best approach?
choices: Apply a hot multi-region design to all services so that no service ever falls below the highest requirement
Use cold backups for every service because the customer-facing availability target is met by the application tier only
Let every application team choose its own pattern and record it in a spreadsheet, then compare totals at year end
Rank services with a business impact analysis, set RTO and RPO per tier, and pick the DR pattern for each tier within budget
quiz.explain: Objectives should come from business impact per service, and tighter objectives cost more, so a tiered design avoids both wasted spend and gaps. A uniform hot design overspends on the reporting job, uniform cold backups fail the claims service, and uncoordinated choices give no consistent target.

days.recap: Move from CapEx to OpEx with budgets, labels and billing export. Attribute first, remove waste with Recommender, then commit to steady load and use Spot VMs for interruptible work. Set RTO and RPO per tier from a business impact analysis and prove them in tests. Domain 4 favors evidence, pilots and measured recovery.

days.title: Deployment Advice: Apigee, Cloud Deploy and Safe Release Testing

concepts.heading: API management is more than hosting an endpoint
concepts.body: A service on Cloud Run answers requests, but an API offered to outside consumers must be run as a product. Apigee adds that layer in front of an existing backend. It gives each registered app its own credentials, so access can be granted or revoked one consumer at a time. It applies traffic policy per app at the proxy, records analytics on who calls which API, how often and with what errors, and lets you publish new proxy revisions or versions through a developer portal without forcing every consumer to change at once. Cymbal Retail shows the pattern. It wants suppliers to submit product data through an interface instead of SFTP file drops, needs to know which supplier calls what, wants a separate allowance for each supplier and expects the API to evolve. Hosting the endpoint alone delivers none of that, while Apigee in front of the service delivers all of it with no change to the backend code. The trade-off is another platform to learn and govern, so it earns its place for external or contractual APIs, not for every internal call.

concepts.heading: Quota, SpikeArrest and ResponseCache solve different problems
concepts.body: Apigee has several policies that sound alike, and the exam separates them by purpose. Quota keeps a distributed counter of the requests a client app may send over an hour, day, week or month, so it enforces a business contract or SLA with a partner. SpikeArrest throttles the rate at which requests reach the backend, so it is an operational control that protects against sudden bursts and the performance lags or downtime they cause. ResponseCache stores backend answers so repeated requests for the same URI never reach the backend, which suits data that changes only periodically. A bank offering a payments API to fintech partners with a monthly allowance per partner and a need to shield the backend from bursts uses both Quota and SpikeArrest. A public transport authority whose timetable changes every ten minutes while thousands of apps request the same routes uses ResponseCache, with a time to live no longer than the staleness the business accepts. Personal or fast-changing data, and payment requests, are poor candidates for caching.

concepts.heading: Apigee fully managed versus Apigee hybrid
concepts.body: Apigee has a management plane, which holds configuration, analytics and the developer portal, and a runtime plane, which processes the API calls. In the fully managed offering Google hosts both planes. In Apigee hybrid the management plane stays hosted by Apigee in the cloud, while the customer installs and operates the runtime plane on a supported Kubernetes platform. Choose hybrid when a rule says that API traffic must be processed in your own facilities or environment, for example a contract with a partner, a security rule or existing governance, while you still want Google-hosted management, analytics and a portal. An insurer exposing claims APIs under such a contract, and already running Kubernetes in its own data center, fits hybrid. The price is operations: in hybrid the customer manages the runtime cluster, its upgrades and its capacity, while in the managed model Google does. So the architect asks whether traffic location is a hard requirement. If it is not, the managed offering is simpler to operate and the default recommendation.

concepts.heading: Cloud Deploy: continuous delivery separate from CI
concepts.body: Cloud Deploy is a managed continuous delivery service. A delivery pipeline defines the promotion sequence of targets, for example dev, then staging, then production. The output of any CI process that produces container images, such as Cloud Build or another tool, can create a release, the release rolls out to the first target, and promoting it moves it to the next one. Pipelines can use approval gates on chosen targets and deployment strategies such as canary, and Cloud Deploy can run verification after a deployment, using a container image with your tests whose exit code decides success or failure. The design value is central, auditable promotion rules while each team keeps its CI choice. Altostrat Media, with several engineering teams delivering containerized services through dev, staging and production, is the typical case: one place defines who must approve production and which strategy applies, instead of a different script per team. Cloud Deploy does not build images and does not provision the platform, which are jobs for Cloud Build and Terraform.

concepts.heading: Release strategies and testing placement
concepts.body: Safe deployment limits the blast radius and keeps a way back. Cloud Run lets you choose which revisions receive traffic and in what percentage, so you can deploy gradually, split traffic and roll back to a previous revision by changing traffic, not by rebuilding; Cloud Deploy can automate the same canary pattern for Cloud Run and GKE targets. A blue/green or canary release breaks down when the new version changes shared state the old version cannot read, such as a database column format, because rollback then fails. The remedy is expand and contract: add the new format while keeping the old, migrate existing data in the background, and remove the old format only after the new version is stable and the rollback window has closed. Tests follow a pyramid. Unit tests run on every commit, integration tests run on merge in an ephemeral environment, and slow load tests run before release or on a schedule in a production-like environment, with a canary rollout verifying behavior on real traffic. The aim is fast feedback early and deeper assurance later.

examPoints: A question about per-partner allowances versus burst protection is testing Quota for contracts over time and SpikeArrest for backend protection, often together.
A question where API traffic must be processed in the customer's own facilities with Google-hosted management is testing Apigee hybrid, whose runtime plane the customer operates.
A question about a rollback that fails after a schema change is testing expand and contract, so that old and new application versions can both read the data.

quiz.q: A logistics company exposes a shipment-tracking API to fifty retail partners. Each contract grants a partner two million calls per month. A bug in one partner's integration sometimes sends thousands of calls within seconds and slows the shared backend for everyone. What should the architect configure in Apigee?
choices: A ResponseCache policy on every proxy, because answering repeated requests from the cache removes both the contract limit and the burst
A SpikeArrest policy configured with a monthly count, because rate throttling is the policy that enforces a partner's contractual allowance
A Quota policy per partner app for the monthly allowance, plus a SpikeArrest policy that limits the request rate reaching the backend
A Quota policy with a very short interval alone, because one counter can serve as both the contract limit and the burst protection
quiz.explain: Quota counts requests per app over hours to months and enforces the contract, while SpikeArrest limits the rate of requests reaching the backend and protects against bursts. SpikeArrest is a rate control, not a monthly counter, and a cache does not enforce limits per caller.

quiz.q: Altostrat Media has five teams that each use a different CI tool to build container images. Leadership wants one central definition of the dev, staging and production sequence, with a manual approval before production and a canary rollout, without forcing teams to change CI. What should the architect advise?
choices: Require every team to move to a single Cloud Build trigger chain that builds, tests and deploys all environments in one configuration file
Define a Cloud Deploy delivery pipeline with an approval gate on the production target, and let any CI tool create releases from its images
Publish each service behind an Apigee proxy and use proxy revisions to move traffic from staging to production after a manager approves
Keep one Terraform configuration per environment and let each team copy the image reference between the files by hand after review
quiz.explain: Cloud Deploy accepts the output of any CI process, defines the promotion order of targets, supports approval gates and canary strategies, and keeps the rules central and auditable. Apigee manages APIs, not container delivery, and hand-copied Terraform files recreate the script-by-script problem.

days.recap: Apigee turns a backend into a managed API product: Quota for contracts, SpikeArrest for bursts, ResponseCache for periodic data, hybrid when the runtime must stay in your facilities. Cloud Deploy promotes releases from any CI through approved targets; use traffic splitting, expand and contract, and a test pyramid.

days.title: Migration and Data Tooling: Transfer, Replicate, Migrate and Get AI Help

concepts.heading: Online or offline transfer of bulk data
concepts.body: The time to move data is its size divided by the bandwidth you can really use. When that figure is weeks or months, or when the link must not be saturated, shipping storage is faster. Storage Transfer Service is the online route: a managed, highly parallelized service with automatic retries, load balancing and integrity validation, moving data between object and file stores, including Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage, on-premises storage and URLs into Cloud Storage. It is optimized for transfers above 1 TiB, can be run repeatedly to pick up new data and removes custom scripts and servers, but it still depends on the network. Transfer Appliance is the offline route: you copy data to a high-capacity device on site, ship it to a Google facility, and Google uploads the data to your bucket and wipes the device. A media company with 200 TiB in Amazon S3 and good bandwidth uses Storage Transfer Service. KnightMotives, with several hundred terabytes at a rural proving ground on a slow shared link that must stay available to plant operations, uses Transfer Appliance.

concepts.heading: Datastream, Database Migration Service and the file movers
concepts.body: Four data-moving tools are easy to confuse, so match each to its job. Datastream is a serverless change data capture and replication service. It reads a database's change log, supports sources such as MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, AlloyDB and Spanner, and replicates into BigQuery for near real-time analytics or writes change streams to Cloud Storage, without repeated queries or custom code on the source. Database Migration Service moves a database to a new managed engine, namely Cloud SQL or AlloyDB, and ends with a promotion of the destination. Storage Transfer Service and Transfer Appliance move files and objects in bulk. Cymbal Retail, whose analysts need MySQL and SQL Server order changes in BigQuery within seconds while the source keeps serving the shop, wants Datastream; the source remains the system of record, so nothing is migrated. A hospital group retiring its self-managed MySQL wants Database Migration Service, because the database itself must move. The question to ask is whether the source stays in service or is replaced.

concepts.heading: Database Migration Service: continuous, homogeneous and heterogeneous
concepts.body: A Database Migration Service job first copies existing data and then keeps replicating changes from the source while the application keeps working. When lag is small you promote the destination to primary and move the application, so downtime is only the cutover window. A dump and import suits small databases that can go offline, but downtime grows with data size, and for very large self-hosted databases the service also supports physical backup files created with Percona XtraBackup. MySQL to Cloud SQL for MySQL is homogeneous: the engine does not change. Oracle to Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL is heterogeneous, so schema, data types, procedures and SQL dialect must be translated. The service provides a conversion workspace that converts the Oracle schema and other objects to PostgreSQL syntax, then a migration job moves the data and the job is promoted. Conversion can leave issues, so the team still fixes the flagged objects, reviews the result and tests application queries and behavior on PostgreSQL. A manufacturer cutting licensing cost by leaving Oracle should plan that extra work as part of the business case.

concepts.heading: Migrate to Virtual Machines and proving the result
concepts.body: Migrate to Virtual Machines migrates VM instances and their disks from sources such as vSphere, AWS, Azure and Google Cloud VMware Engine to Compute Engine instances or Persistent Disk volumes. It is a rehost, or lift and shift: the operating system and software stay as they are. That suits packaged or licensed software that cannot be changed, such as a legacy on-premises ingestion server of Altostrat Media if it is of that kind, and it keeps effort and outage per server small. The trade-off is that the workload gets few cloud-native benefits until it is modernized later, so the plan should name the next step. The other approaches, ordered from least to most change, are replatform, refactor or re-architect, rebuild and repurchase. Whatever the approach, readiness for cutover is shown by evidence. Validate data by comparing counts, checksums or samples of critical tables and by confirming that replication lag is near zero. Validate behavior by running application test suites and representative query workloads on the destination. Keep the source until the destination is proven, as the rollback path.

concepts.heading: Gemini Cloud Assist for design and troubleshooting
concepts.body: Gemini Cloud Assist is an AI collaborator across the application lifecycle: designing, deploying, troubleshooting and optimizing. For design it helps in natural language, including in Application Design Center, and can iteratively generate or refine Terraform, gcloud commands and kubectl manifests using context such as your project and organization. For troubleshooting it offers investigations, which ingest logs, metrics and configuration, explore hypotheses in parallel and trace root causes across multi-tier topologies. An alerting policy can also trigger a proactive alert investigation: it analyzes the issue in the background, clusters related alerts and produces a preliminary root-cause analysis with recommended next steps, and the results can be handed to Google Cloud support. EHR Healthcare, whose past outages were prolonged by ignored email alerts, is the natural fit. The architect's advice has two halves. The tool builds on signals you already collect and does not replace alert definitions or human judgment. Generated infrastructure code is a proposal, so it goes through version control, peer review, policy and security checks and a staged pipeline like any contributor's change.

examPoints: A question about hundreds of terabytes on a slow or shared link is testing Transfer Appliance, while good bandwidth and a cloud source point to Storage Transfer Service.
A question about near real-time database changes in BigQuery with no load on the source is testing Datastream, not Database Migration Service.
A question about leaving Oracle for PostgreSQL is testing a heterogeneous Database Migration Service job with a conversion workspace plus manual review and testing.

quiz.q: A research hospital has 600 TiB of imaging archives on storage in its own data center. The internet link is shared with clinical systems and can spare only a small fraction of its capacity, so an online copy would take many months. The archive must be in Cloud Storage within weeks. What should the architect recommend?
choices: Run Storage Transfer Service over the existing link with the bandwidth limit raised, because the managed service removes the network constraint
Copy the data to a Transfer Appliance on site, ship it to Google for upload to the bucket, and use online transfer only for later changes
Stream the archive with Datastream into Cloud Storage, because it replicates continuously without adding load on the clinical systems
Use Database Migration Service to move the archives, because it validates integrity and promotes the destination once the copy is done
quiz.explain: When size divided by usable bandwidth exceeds the deadline or would harm other traffic, shipping a Transfer Appliance is faster. Storage Transfer Service still depends on the network, Datastream captures database changes, and Database Migration Service moves databases, not file archives.

quiz.q: KnightMotives will retire its on-premises PostgreSQL dealer-order database and run it on Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. Dealers can accept only a short outage at cutover. Which approach fits?
choices: Datastream replicating changes into BigQuery, then repointing the dealer application at the BigQuery tables on the cutover day, with no other work
Migrate to Virtual Machines to move the database server to Compute Engine as it is, then convert the instance to Cloud SQL at some later date
A nightly dump of the database copied to Cloud Storage and imported into Cloud SQL during a long weekend maintenance window for the dealers
A Database Migration Service migration job that copies existing data, replicates ongoing changes, and is promoted when lag is small
quiz.explain: A continuous Database Migration Service job keeps the destination in sync and limits downtime to the cutover window. Datastream feeds analytics rather than a new primary, a dump and import grows downtime with data size, and rehosting the VM does not produce a managed Cloud SQL database.

days.recap: Pick the mover by the job: Storage Transfer Service for online bulk objects, Transfer Appliance when bandwidth cannot meet the deadline, Datastream for continuous change capture, Database Migration Service to replace a database, Migrate to Virtual Machines to rehost. Prove cutover with data and behavior checks.

days.title: Programmatic Access: Tooling, Emulators, Terraform and Credentials

concepts.heading: Cloud Shell, Cloud Workstations and Cloud Code
concepts.body: Both Cloud Shell and Cloud Workstations keep tools off a personal laptop and are reached from a browser, but they answer different needs. Cloud Shell gives every user a free, pre-configured environment: an ephemeral Debian-based VM owned and managed by Google, with the gcloud CLI, Git, Docker, Terraform and editors, discarded after an hour of inactivity but with a 5 GB persistent home directory. You cannot choose its machine type, image or network. Cloud Workstations gives managed development environments on Compute Engine VMs in your own project, defined by an administrator through a workstation configuration (VM type, container image, IDE, disk, idle timeout) and attached to your VPC network, so every developer gets an identical, centrally governed environment. For thirty short-term contractors on unmanaged laptops who must work against a client's projects under client control, Cloud Workstations is the answer; Cloud Shell is the quick personal option. Cloud Code is the third piece: extensions for VS Code, IntelliJ and Cloud Shell that shorten the inner loop for Kubernetes and Cloud Run applications, while Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy form the outer delivery loop.

concepts.heading: The command-line tools and client libraries
concepts.body: The Google Cloud CLI is a family. The gcloud command manages most services, and gcloud storage is its command group for Cloud Storage buckets and objects. gsutil is an older Python tool for Cloud Storage that the documentation calls a legacy CLI, minimally maintained; existing gsutil runbooks keep working, so there is no emergency rewrite, but new automation should use gcloud storage and old scripts can migrate as they are touched. The bq tool is for BigQuery datasets, tables, queries and loads, not for Cloud Storage objects. For large recurring transfers from other sources a managed service such as Storage Transfer Service beats any script. When code, not a shell, calls Google Cloud APIs there are three ways. Cloud Client Libraries are the recommended option: idiomatic per language, consistent across services, handling authentication and low-level communication, and in some cases using gRPC, which can raise throughput per CPU over JSON over REST. Google API Client Libraries are older, REST only and less idiomatic, kept for languages or APIs without a Cloud Client Library. Hand-written REST is for rare cases the libraries do not meet.

concepts.heading: Emulators for fast, isolated tests
concepts.body: The Google Cloud CLI ships local, in-memory emulators for services such as Spanner, Pub/Sub, Bigtable and Firestore. The same client library code runs against them, usually switched by an environment variable such as PUBSUB_EMULATOR_HOST or FIRESTORE_EMULATOR_HOST, so application code is identical in test and production, tests need no project, credentials or billing, and every run starts clean. That makes them ideal for functional tests on each commit in CI. They are not production substitutes. Data, schema and configuration vanish when the emulator restarts, performance and scalability do not compare to the real service, and error messages can differ. The Spanner emulator does not verify whether a statement is really partitionable. The Bigtable emulator provides no instance administration and no secure connection. The Pub/Sub emulator is for applications built with Cloud Client Libraries: the console and gcloud pubsub commands talk to the real service and are not supported with it. The architect's rule is to use emulators for fast functional tests and keep a smaller stage on the real service for performance, quotas, IAM, replication and failover. A hand-written fake tests the fake, and production data in tests risks exposure.

concepts.heading: Terraform as the provisioning path
concepts.body: Terraform lets you declare the desired end state, preview changes with an execution plan and package common patterns as modules. Deploying one configuration several times gives reproducible development, test and production environments, which answers EHR Healthcare's history of outages from misconfiguration: a new region becomes a new set of variable values, not a new project of manual work. Google's best practices shape modules: every variable has a description, environment-independent values get defaults, and environment-specific variables such as project_id have no default, so a forgotten value fails the plan instead of silently targeting production. State maps the configuration to real resources, so a change made by hand is drift; run plan regularly, treat a difference as a finding to import, code or revert, grant routine write access only to the pipeline and use time-bound, audited break-glass access. Renaming a resource block makes Terraform plan a destroy and create, which is data loss for a database, so enable deletion protection, review plans for destroy and replace, use a moved block and keep tested backups. Provisioner scripts sit outside state and should be rare.

concepts.heading: Credentials for code: ADC, attached accounts and federation
concepts.body: Application Default Credentials is how authentication libraries find credentials in the environment, so the same code works in development and production. It searches the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS variable, then a credential file created by gcloud auth application-default login, then the attached service account from the metadata server. In production on Google Cloud the attached, user-managed service account with least-privilege roles is the preferred method, as for a Cloud Run service or a Compute Engine batch job. Service account keys are a security risk and not recommended, because a leaked key works for anyone holding it. Workloads outside Google Cloud, such as Altostrat Media's on-premises ingestion servers with an OpenID Connect provider, use Workload Identity Federation: they exchange an external credential for short-lived access, and a credential configuration file read through ADC means no code change. On a laptop gcloud login does not give libraries credentials; run the application-default login, or impersonate a service account without a key. A standard API key identifies a project for quota, not a principal: acceptable only for public, low-risk data.

examPoints: A question about contractors who need identical, centrally governed environments in the client's own project is testing Cloud Workstations rather than Cloud Shell.
A question about local tests that need no credentials and start clean is testing the emulators, with a real-service stage kept for performance, IAM and replication.
A question about authenticating a production workload without downloading keys is testing the attached service account through ADC, or Workload Identity Federation outside Google Cloud.

quiz.q: A team runs a Cloud Run service that publishes to Pub/Sub. A developer proposes creating a service account key, storing it in Secret Manager and mounting it in the container so the client library can find it. What should the architect recommend instead?
choices: Keep the key but rotate it monthly, because a rotated key is the recommended production credential for services running on Cloud Run
Replace the key with an API key restricted to the Pub/Sub API, because API keys authenticate the service for IAM-controlled actions
Attach a user-managed service account with a least-privilege Pub/Sub role to the service and let Application Default Credentials find it
Use the developers' own user credentials through gcloud auth login in the container, because the library will then discover them
quiz.explain: On Google Cloud the attached service account is the preferred ADC source: no key to store, leak or rotate. Service account keys are discouraged, and an API key identifies a project for quota and cannot be authorized with IAM.

quiz.q: A team has fast Bigtable emulator tests for its time-series access code. The release manager asks whether passing them also shows that cluster replication, failover and IAM restrictions work. How should the architect answer?
choices: Yes, because the emulator models replication between clusters and enforces IAM, so a pass shows the production topology behaves
Yes, if the emulator is started with the production instance name, because the name makes it replicate the real cluster configuration
No, because the emulator runs only inside Cloud Shell, so its results cannot be trusted anywhere outside that environment
No, because the emulator has no persistence, instance administration or secure connection, so those need a test on a real instance
quiz.explain: The Bigtable emulator is in-memory, offers no administrative APIs to create or manage instances and clusters, and has no secure connection, so replication, failover and IAM restrictions cannot be exercised in it. It suits data access tests only; topology, authorization and capacity belong on a real test instance.

days.recap: Use Cloud Workstations for governed environments and Cloud Shell for quick personal access; gcloud storage over gsutil and Cloud Client Libraries over hand-written REST; emulators for fast functional tests only; Terraform modules with no environment defaults, drift checks and guards for stateful resources; ADC with attached accounts or federation, not keys.

days.title: Solution and Operations Excellence: Observe, Release, Support and Prove Reliability

concepts.heading: Operational readiness and incident management
concepts.body: The operational excellence pillar of the Well-Architected Framework asks you to ensure operational readiness and performance using CloudOps. Readiness has four focus areas: workforce (roles, skills, learning), processes (observability, service disruptions, delivery, core operations), tooling and governance (service levels, cloud financials, the operating model, review boards, compliance). KnightMotives, with a large hybrid program and teams new to Google Cloud, should cover all four before go-live. SLOs are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound (SMART), such as 99.9% availability, with SLIs as the measuring metrics and SLAs as the contract. Incident management is prepared in advance: an incident commander, investigators and a communicator, escalation paths, runbooks, one central tracker and post-incident reviews in a blameless culture that looks for systemic causes, not culprits. EHR Healthcare's ignored alerts and unclear ownership are the gaps these close. Repeatable, safe responses, like a documented restart, can be automated by sending an alert to Pub/Sub, where a Cloud Run function acts with least privilege, while the recurring cause still goes into the problem backlog.

concepts.heading: Choosing the right observability signal
concepts.body: Match the signal to the question. Cloud Monitoring metrics show aggregate behavior over time, and averages hide the slow minority. Cloud Logging records events. Cloud Trace tracks request latency across services and shows which downstream call causes delay, which is the answer for Cymbal Retail's slow checkout when each service's average looks normal. Cloud Profiler continuously gathers CPU and memory-allocation data from production with low overhead and attributes it to code, so it shows which functions consume resources. Uptime checks probe endpoints from multiple locations and measure the customer's path, including DNS and load balancer problems healthy servers never show. Error Reporting groups stack traces into error groups with counts and first-seen times, so a new group after a release points to a regression. A log-based metric turns log content into a counter or distribution with no code change, for example timeouts per minute. Logs Explorer finds entries but cannot aggregate; Observability Analytics runs SQL over a log bucket for counts and joins with trace data. Managed Service for Prometheus keeps PromQL and Grafana without running Prometheus servers, and an aggregated sink centralizes logs.

concepts.heading: Alerting that people act on
concepts.body: An alert is useful only if the responder can act on it. Alerting on every cause, such as any VM above 70% CPU for a minute, produces dozens of pages that need no action while a real checkout outage pages nobody. Alert on symptoms and on SLO budget burn instead. A burn rate above 1 means the service will miss its SLO for the period if sustained. Google recommends two policies: a fast-burn alert with a short lookback for sudden large consumption, which pages immediately, and a slow-burn alert with a longer lookback for steady erosion, which opens a ticket or uses lower urgency. A retest window, the condition duration, stops a single measurement from firing the alert, long enough to cut false positives yet short enough to alert in time. Alerting policies can carry Markdown documentation with variables, such as resource labels, plus the runbook link, so whoever is paged knows what to check, and one owner should be named per alert. When your own dashboards look healthy but customers in a region fail, Personalized Service Health shows Google Cloud incidents relevant to your projects, with a dashboard, an API and log-based alerts by product or location.

concepts.heading: Release management and controlled change
concepts.body: Good release management lowers risk and speeds recovery. Config Sync is a GitOps service included with GKE that syncs namespaces, network policies and role bindings from Git to many clusters, on Google Cloud or registered elsewhere, and reverts manual drift, so a revert in Git is a rollback in every cluster. During GKE node upgrades a PodDisruptionBudget keeps a minimum number of replicas available while nodes drain; a budget allowing zero disruption can stall upgrades. For Standard node pools, surge upgrades are the default and cannot be rolled back after completion, while blue-green upgrades keep the original nodes during a soak time at roughly double the node resources, which suits highly available production workloads where quick rollback matters. In managed instance groups, maxSurge and maxUnavailable control rolling updates, and an application-based health check keeps unready VMs out of service. Feature flags separate deployment from release. Artifact Registry cleanup policies delete old artifacts, and a keep rule wins over a delete rule. Cloud Deploy verification gates promotion on test results. DORA metrics balance speed and stability: deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and recovery time.

concepts.heading: Proving reliability: chaos, load, failover, restore and penetration tests
concepts.body: The reliability pillar's message is that recovery is proven only by exercising it. Chaos engineering is controlled experimentation: define scope and objectives, prepare a production-like environment or safety measures, start with small failures and escalate gradually, observe with Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Logging, fix findings, and repeat. A Cloud SQL high-availability instance should have a failover started by hand to see how the application reconnects, measuring request failures and pool recovery against the recovery target. Backups are proven by restoring them into a non-production environment, testing the whole application stack and judging data integrity, RTO and RPO, because a successful job status only proves a file was written. Load tests model real behavior, ramp past the expected peak and watch the whole path, including dependencies that cannot scale like KnightMotives' mainframe ERP; a fast stub hides the likeliest bottleneck. A queue such as Cloud Tasks levels bursts for a fixed-capacity dependency, with idempotent handlers because delivery is at least once. Penetration tests cover only resources you own, should include the DR environment, test detection and response, and are coordinated with operations.

examPoints: A question about slow requests with normal average latency across several services is testing Cloud Trace, while unexplained CPU or memory use inside code is testing Cloud Profiler.
A question about too many pages and a missed outage is testing symptom-based SLO alerts, with fast burn paging and slow burn opening a ticket.
A question about a backup never restored or a failover never seen is testing the reliability pillar rule that recovery is proven by exercising it.

quiz.q: Cymbal Retail defines a 99.9% SLO for checkout success. On-call staff want to be woken only when customers are really being hurt, while a slow, steady rise in failures should still be noticed during working hours. Which alerting design fits?
choices: Page whenever any single pod's CPU exceeds a fixed percentage for one minute, and rely on the pager history to reveal any slow trends over time
Two burn-rate alerts on the SLO: a fast-burn policy with a short lookback that pages, and a slow-burn policy with a longer lookback that opens a ticket
One uptime check against the home page, because a passing check proves that checkout success stays inside the SLO at all times and for every user
A daily email summary of error counts for the whole project, because aggregated reports avoid the false positives that short spikes would produce
quiz.explain: Fast-burn and slow-burn alerts on the SLO tie urgency to customer impact: sudden budget consumption pages, steady erosion creates a ticket. Cause-based CPU alerts are noisy and can miss real outages, and a home-page uptime check does not measure checkout success.

quiz.q: A Go service on Compute Engine restarts every night after its memory grows steadily. Request latency is normal, no single request fails, and the lab cannot reproduce the growth. The team needs to know which functions allocate the memory, without slowing production noticeably. What should the architect recommend?
choices: Enable Cloud Profiler on the service to gather allocation profiles continuously from production and attribute them to source code
Add a Cloud Trace sampling policy, because traces show which function allocates memory inside each individual request across the service
Create an uptime check on the public endpoint, because failed probes identify the functions that slowly leak memory over a whole day
Turn on Error Reporting, because grouped stack traces show where the process allocates memory in its last minutes before it restarts
quiz.explain: Cloud Profiler is a low-overhead statistical profiler that collects CPU and memory-allocation data from production and attributes it to code. Trace follows request paths across services, uptime checks measure external availability and Error Reporting groups errors, none of which show allocations.

days.recap: Operational excellence means readiness (workforce, processes, tooling, governance), prepared incident handling and symptom-based SLO alerts. Choose Trace, Profiler, uptime checks or log analytics by the question. Release with drift control, PDBs and rollback paths, and prove reliability by chaos, load, failover, restore and pen tests.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Case Studies, Confused Pairs and Test Day

concepts.heading: Exam format and what each section rewards
concepts.body: The Professional Cloud Architect exam lasts 2 hours and has 50-60 multiple choice and multiple select questions. The pass mark is not published, so aim for solid command of every section. Two case studies appear, and together they make up 20-30% of the questions. The sections by weight are: design and plan a cloud solution architecture, about 25%; manage and provision the cloud solution infrastructure, 17.5%; design for security and compliance, 17.5%; analyze and optimize technical and business processes, 15%; manage implementation, 12.5%; and ensure solution and operations excellence, 12.5%. Questions test the architect's choice, which design and why, against business and technical requirements such as availability, cost, latency, compliance and migration effort, so commands matter little. The Well-Architected Framework pillars (operational excellence, security, reliability, performance optimization, cost optimization, sustainability) frame the answers, and the exam guide's product names apply: Agent Platform, Gemini Cloud Assist, Model Armor, Chrome Enterprise Premium, Migration Center and Cloud Run functions. Two hours for up to 60 questions leaves about two minutes each.

concepts.heading: The four case studies and how to read them
concepts.body: Four case studies are published and two appear on your exam. Altostrat Media is a media company with a large audio and video library in Cloud Storage, a BigQuery warehouse, GKE and Cloud Run functions, legacy on-premises ingestion, and needs for hybrid connectivity, storage cost with high availability, auditable and explainable AI, and harmful-content detection. Cymbal Retail is a fast-growing online retailer with MySQL, SQL Server, Redis and MongoDB, SFTP and batch ETL integrations, open source monitoring, and wants gen AI for catalog enrichment and conversational commerce with human review. EHR Healthcare is a SaaS health-records company leaving colocation, needing at least 99.9% availability, legacy insurer interfaces, consistent logging and monitoring, and compliance. KnightMotives Automotive is a car maker with an unreliable build-to-order system, a mainframe ERP, past breaches, EU data protection duties, weak plant connectivity and a hybrid strategy. Read the business goal and the technical requirements first, find the single fact that decides the question, such as a hard availability number, a legacy dependency or a compliance duty, and answer for that case only. Do not import facts from another case.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs: network, compute, data and storage
concepts.body: Shared VPC gives one organization central network control with delegated workload projects; VPC Network Peering joins separately run networks, is not transitive and needs non-overlapping ranges. HA VPN is quick and encrypted over the internet; Dedicated Interconnect gives dedicated capacity off the internet; Partner Interconnect reaches Google through a provider; Cross-Cloud Interconnect links to another cloud. Regional dynamic routing advertises only the Cloud Router's region; global advertises all regions. Passthrough Network Load Balancers keep client IP and handle UDP; proxy load balancers terminate connections, and the global Application Load Balancer adds URL routing, Cloud CDN and Cloud Armor. A hybrid connectivity NEG reaches on-premises endpoints privately; an internet NEG goes over the internet. GKE Autopilot is managed with restrictions; Standard gives node-level control. Cloud SQL scales reads but writes in one primary; Spanner offers relational, strongly consistent multi-region; Bigtable is wide-column and asynchronous. Soft delete restores for 7 to 90 days; versioning keeps noncurrent versions; a retention policy blocks deletion; Bucket Lock makes it permanent. Cold, warm and hot DR trade RTO and RPO against cost.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs: security and compliance
concepts.body: IAM decides who may call an API; VPC Service Controls draws a perimeter that stops exfiltration even by principals with valid roles, and Google recommends both. IAM allow policies grant; deny policies override allow and apply down the hierarchy; organization policy restricts what resources may be configured. Preventive controls such as organization policy refuse the action; detective controls such as Security Command Center find drift. Workforce Identity Federation is for people from an external IdP; Workload Identity Federation is for software outside Google Cloud. Cloud KMS Admin manages keys but cannot encrypt or decrypt, while the Encrypter/Decrypter role uses them. Cloud HSM keeps keys in Google-run hardware; Cloud EKM keeps them externally, so availability depends on you. Access Transparency logs what Google personnel did; Access Approval requires your approval first. The resource locations constraint covers data residency; Assured Workloads adds control packages, including support access by EU personnel. IAP gates web apps by identity; Chrome Enterprise Premium adds device and context through the browser. Sensitive Data Protection de-identifies data; Model Armor screens prompts and responses.

concepts.heading: Confused pairs: delivery, migration, operations and a test-day plan
concepts.body: Quota enforces a contract; SpikeArrest limits rate; ResponseCache saves backend calls. Apigee hybrid keeps the runtime in your facilities. Cloud Build builds and tests; Cloud Deploy promotes releases with approvals. Storage Transfer Service moves data online; Transfer Appliance ships it. Datastream replicates changes while the source stays; Database Migration Service replaces the database, with a conversion workspace when the engine changes. Rehost changes nothing; replatform adopts some cloud features; refactor and rebuild change the workload; repurchase buys SaaS. Resource-based commitments fit steady use; compute flexible ones fit shifting use. Trace follows a request across services; Profiler shows code consumption; uptime checks measure the customer's path; Error Reporting groups errors; Logs Explorer finds entries while Observability Analytics aggregates them. Fast burn pages; slow burn opens a ticket. A backup is proven by a restore. On test day, read the last sentence of the stem first, underline hard constraints (RTO, residency, minimal change, lowest operations), eliminate options that break one, and prefer managed services when nothing forbids them. Flag long case questions, finish the rest, and return with time left.

examPoints: The exam has 50-60 multiple choice and multiple select questions in 2 hours, an unpublished pass mark, and two case studies making up 20-30% of the questions.
Case study questions turn on one decisive fact from the named business, so read the goal and the technical requirement and answer for that case only.
Most wrong options fail one stated constraint, so the fastest method is to mark each hard requirement and discard the choices that break it.

quiz.q: A finance company's analyst holds valid IAM roles on a BigQuery dataset. Security requires that even such a user, or a thief using the analyst's valid credentials, cannot export the data to a bucket in another organization's project. Which control addresses this requirement?
choices: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the project, with ingress and egress rules opened only for approved exchanges
An IAM allow policy that removes the export permission from the analyst, because allow policies override any other control
An organization policy on resource locations, because limiting regions prevents data from reaching another organization
A Cloud KMS key with the Encrypter/Decrypter role withheld, because encryption stops any copy from leaving the dataset
quiz.explain: VPC Service Controls adds a perimeter that blocks reads and writes of protected services across its boundary even for principals with the right roles, and it is used together with IAM. Allow policies grant rather than limit destinations, and resource locations govern regions, not recipients.

quiz.q: Contractors of a Cymbal Retail merchandising partner sign in with their own company's SAML identity provider. They need access to Google Cloud resources, and the retailer does not want to create or synchronize a Google account for each person. What should the architect use?
choices: Workload Identity Federation, because it exchanges an external identity for short-lived access and so suits any kind of human principal as well
A service account key shared by the contractors, because a single key avoids creating individual accounts for every person who needs access
Workforce Identity Federation, whose workforce identity pool maps IdP claims to principals that IAM policies can reference directly
An API key restricted to the required APIs, because keys identify each contractor to IAM without any account or sign-in at all
quiz.explain: Workforce Identity Federation is for people who sign in with an external OIDC or SAML provider and are mapped to a workforce identity pool, with no Google account per person. Workload Identity Federation is for software outside Google Cloud, and keys, whether service account or API, are the wrong credential for people.

days.recap: Exam: 2 hours, 50-60 questions, pass mark unpublished, two case studies at 20-30%. Read each case for the one decisive fact. Review the confused pairs across network, data, security, delivery and operations, then on test day mark hard constraints, eliminate what breaks them and prefer managed services.
